description: Abstract With the rising use of Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) in various industries, the medical industry is also not far behind. A very simple yet extremely important use case of ML in this industry is for image classification.

title: The Fragmented Glueball: A Personal View
creator: \firstname Eberhard \lastname Klempt \fnsep
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by \firstname Eberhard \lastname Klempt \fnsep. A coupled-channel analysis has been performed to identify the spectrum of scalar mesons. The data include BESIII data on radiative J / ψ J/\psi decays into π 0 ​ π 0 \pi^{0}\pi^{0} , K S ​ K S K_{S}K_{S} , η ​ η \eta\eta , and ω ​ ϕ \omega\phi , 15 Dalitz plots from p ¯ ​ N \bar{p}N annihilation at rest at LEAR, the CERN-Munich multipoles for π ​ π \pi\pi elastic scattering, the S S -wave

title: A scoring framework for tiered warnings and multicategorical forecasts based on fixed risk measures
creator: Robert Taggart, Nicholas Loveday, Deryn Griffiths
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Robert Taggart, Nicholas Loveday, Deryn Griffiths. The use of tiered warnings and multicategorical forecasts are ubiquitous in meteorological operations. Here, a flexible family of scoring functions is presented for evaluating the performance of ordered multicategorical forecasts. Each score has a risk parameter α \alpha , selected for the specific use case, so that it is consistent with a forecast directive based on the fixed threshold probability 1 − α 1-\alpha (equivalently, a fixed α \alpha -quantile mapping).

title: Analyzing and Mitigating Interference in Neural Architecture Search
creator: Jin Xu, Xu Tan, Kaitao Song, Renqian Luo, Yichong Leng, Tao Qin, Tie-Yan Liu, Jian Li
description: Abstract Weight sharing is a popular approach to reduce the cost of neural architecture search (NAS) by reusing the weights of shared operators from previously trained child models. However, the rank correlation between the estimated accuracy and ground truth accuracy of those child models is low due to the interference among different child models caused by weight sharing.

title: Black to white transition of a charged black hole
creator: Antoine Rignon-Bret, Carlo Rovelli
description: Abstract We present an exact solution of the Maxwell-Einstein equations, which describes the exterior of a charged spherical mass collapsing into its own trapping horizon and then bouncing back from an anti-trapping horizon at the same space location of the same asymptotic region.

title: A Survey and Comparative Study on Multi-Cloud Architectures: Emerging Issues and Challenges for Cloud Federation
creator: Deepika Saxena, Rishabh Gupta, Ashutosh Kumar Singh
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Deepika Saxena, Rishabh Gupta, Ashutosh Kumar Singh. Multi-cloud concept has broaden the world of cloud computing and has become a buzzword today. The word “Multi-cloud” envisions utilization of services from multiple heterogeneous cloud providers via a single architecture at customer (e.g. organization) premises. Though cloud computing has many issues and offers open research challenges, still the academics and industrial research has paved a pathway for multi-cloud environment.

title: Phonon signatures in spectra of exciton polaritons in transition metal dichalcogenides
creator: F. Lengers, T. Kuhn, D. E. Reiter
description: Abstract Embedding a monolayer of a transition metal dichalcogenide in a high-Q optical cavity results in the formation of distinct exciton polariton modes. The polaritons are affected by the strong exciton-phonon interaction in the monolayer. We use a time convolutionless master equation to calculate the phonon influence on the spectra of the polaritons.

title: Restricted Positional Games
creator: Pranav Avadhanam, Siddhartha G. Jena
description: Abstract 1 Introduction A (two-player) strong positional game played on a hypergraph (X,H) ( H being a collection of subsets of X ) is a game where two players sequentially label(“claim”) vertices of X with colors assigned to each player until all vertices of the board are claimed(see [ Kri14 ] for a thorough introduction to positional games).

title: Topological properties of non-Hermitian Creutz Ladders
creator: Hui-Qiang Liang, Linhu Li
description: Abstract In this work we study topological properties of the one-dimensional Creutz ladder model with different non-Hermitian asymmetric hoppings and on-site imaginary potentials, and obtain phase diagrams regarding the presence and absence of an energy gap and in-gap edge modes.

title: Flow-Guided Video Inpainting with Scene Templates
creator: Dong Lao Peihao Zhu Peter Wonka Ganesh Sundaramoorthi
description: Abstract We consider the problem of filling in missing spatio-temporal regions of a video. We provide a novel flow-based solution by introducing a generative model of images in relation to the scene (without missing regions) and mappings from the scene to images.

title: Span Fine-tuning for Pre-trained Language Models
creator: Rongzhou Bao, Zhuosheng Zhang, Hai Zhao
description: Abstract Pre-trained language models (PrLM) have to carefully manage input units when training on a very large text with a vocabulary consisting of millions of words. Previous works have shown that incorporating span-level information over consecutive words in pre-training could further improve the performance of PrLMs.

title: A Refinement of Carlson’s Theorem
creator: Armen Vagharshakyan
description: Abstract Carlson’s theorem estimates the growth of an analytic function along the imaginary axis, provided that the function is zero at non-negative integers. We refine this theorem and describe not only the function’s growth but also necessary and sufficient conditions in terms of its spectral measure.

title: Exact algorithms for maximum weighted independent set on sparse graphs
creator: Sen Huang, Mingyu Xiao, Xiaoyu Chen
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Sen Huang, Mingyu Xiao, Xiaoyu Chen. The maximum independent set problem is one of the most important problems in graph algorithms and has been extensively studied in the line of research on the worst-case analysis of exact algorithms for NP-hard problems. In the weighted version, each vertex in the graph is associated with a weight and we are going to find an independent set of maximum total vertex weight.

title: Non-Parametric Neural Style Transfer
creator: Nicholas Isaac Kolkin
description: Abstract It seems easy to imagine a photograph of the Eiffel Tower painted in the style of Vincent van Gogh’s ’The Starry Night’, but upon introspection it is difficult to precisely define what this would entail. What visual elements must an image contain to represent the ’content’ of the Eiffel Tower?

title: Differentiable Convolution Search for Point Cloud Processing
creator: Xing Nie, Yongcheng Liu, Shaohong Chen, Jianlong Chang, Chunlei Huo, Gaofeng Meng, Qi Tian, Weiming Hu, Chunhong Pan, [0.2cm] National Laboratory of Pattern Recognition, Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences
description: Abstract Exploiting convolutional neural networks for point cloud processing is quite challenging, due to the inherent irregular distribution and discrete shape representation of point clouds. To address these problems, many handcrafted convolution variants have sprung up in recent years. Though with elaborate design, these variants could be far from optimal in sufficiently capturing diverse shapes formed by discrete points.

title: 3-form Yang-Mills based on 2-crossed modules
creator: Danhua Song, Kai Lou, Ke Wu, Jie Yang, Fuhao Zhang
description: Abstract In this paper, we study the higher Yang-Mills theory in the framework of higher gauge theory. It was shown that the 2-form electromagnetism can be generalized to the 2-form Yang-Mills theory with the group U ⁡ ( 1 ) U(1) replaced by a crossed module of Lie groups.

title: Keller-type bounds for Dirac operators perturbed by rigid potentials
creator: Haruya Mizutani and Nico M. Schiavone
description: Abstract In this paper we are interested in generalizing Keller-type eigenvalue estimates for the non-selfadjoint Schrödinger operator to the Dirac operator, imposing some suitable rigidity conditions on the matricial structure of the potential, without necessarily requiring the smallness of its norm.

title: Lower Bounds for the MMSE via Neural Network Estimation and Their Applications to Privacy
creator: Mario Diaz, Peter Kairouz, and Lalitha Sankar
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Mario Diaz, Peter Kairouz, and Lalitha Sankar. The minimum mean-square error (MMSE) achievable by optimal estimation of a random variable Y ∈ ℝ Y\in\mathbb{R} given another random variable X ∈ ℝ d X\in\mathbb{R}^{d} is of much interest in a variety of statistical settings. In the context of estimation-theoretic privacy, the MMSE has been proposed as an information leakage measure that captures the ability of an adversary in estimating Y Y upon observing X X .

title: Neural Network Gaussian Processes by Increasing Depth
creator: Shao-Qun Zhang, Fei Wang, Senior Member, IEEE, Feng-Lei Fan, Member, IEEE
description: Abstract Recent years have witnessed an increasing interest in the correspondence between infinitely wide networks and Gaussian processes. Despite the effectiveness and elegance of the current neural network Gaussian process theory, to the best of our knowledge, all the neural network Gaussian processes are essentially induced by increasing width.

title: MBDF-Net: Multi-Branch Deep Fusion Network for 3D Object Detection Thanks: ✉ Corresponding author CCS: Computing methodologies Vision for robotics CCS: Computing methodologies Scene understanding
creator: Xun Tan 1 , Xingyu Chen 1 , Guowei Zhang 1 , Jishiyu Ding 2 , Xuguang Lan 1, ✉
description: Abstract . Point clouds and images could provide complementary information when representing 3D objects. Fusing the two kinds of data usually helps to improve the detection results. However, it is challenging to fuse the two data modalities, due to their different characteristics and the interference from the non-interest areas.

title: A Multimodal Framework for Video Ads Understanding Conference: Proceedings of the 29th ACM International Conference on Multimedia; October 20–24, 2021; Virtual Event, China Proceedings of the 29th ACM International Conference on Multimedia (MM ’21), October 20–24, 2021, Virtual Event, China Price: 1
creator: Zejia Weng, Lingchen Meng, Rui Wang, Zuxuan Wu, Yu-Gang Jiang
description: Abstract . There is a growing trend in placing video advertisements on social platforms for online marketing, which demands automatic approaches to understand the contents of advertisements effectively. Taking the 2021 TAAC competition as an opportunity, we developed a multimodal system to improve the ability of structured analysis of advertising video content.

title: Multiplex Graph Neural Network for Extractive Text Summarization
creator: Baoyu Jing, Zeyu You, Tao Yang, Wei Fan, Hanghang Tong
description: Abstract Extractive text summarization aims at extracting the most representative sentences from a given document as its summary. To extract a good summary from a long text document, sentence embedding plays an important role. Recent studies have leveraged graph neural networks to capture the inter-sentential relationship (e.g., the discourse graph) to learn contextual sentence embedding.

title: Solving Viewing Graph Optimization for Simultaneous Position and Rotation Registration
creator: Seyed-Mahdi Nasiri, Reshad Hosseini, Hadi Moradi
description: Abstract A viewing graph is a set of unknown camera poses, as the vertices, and the observed relative motions, as the edges. Solving the viewing graph is an essential step in a Structure-from-Motion procedure, where a set of relative motions is obtained from a collection of 2D images.

title: Fractional entropy of multichannel Kondo systems from conductance-charge relations: Supplemental Material
creator: Cheolhee Han, Z. Iftikhar, Yaakov Kleeorin, A. Anthore, F. Pierre, Yigal Meir, Andrew K. Mitchell, Eran Sela
description: Abstract I Charge-2CK model: bosonization and refermionization We start with the original model for the charge Kondo system in Eq. (1) of the main paper. The electron number operator of the QD is defined as, \hat{N}=\sum_{j=1}^{k}\int_{0}^{\infty}dx[\psi^{\dagger}_{j\text{in}}(x)\psi_{j\text{in}}(x)+\psi^{\dagger}_{j\text{out}}(-x)\psi_{j\text{out}}(-x)]. (1) The range corresponding to the QD is 0<x<\infty for the incoming modes and from -\infty<x<0 for the outgoing modes.

title: Parameterizing the Permanent: Hardness for K 8 K_{8} -minor-free graphs
creator: Radu Curticapean Mingji Xia
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Radu Curticapean Mingji Xia. In the 1960s, statistical physicists discovered a fascinating algorithm for counting perfect matchings in planar graphs. Valiant later showed that the same problem is # ​ 𝖯 \mathsf{\#P} -hard for general graphs.

title: Phonon-assisted carrier cooling in h h -BN/graphene van der Waals heterostructures
creator: Sangkha Borah, Dinesh Yadav, Maxim Trushin, Fabian Pauly
description: Abstract Being used in optoelectronic devices as ultra-thin conductor-insulator junctions, detailed investigations are needed about how exactly h h -BN and graphene hybridize. Here, we present a comprehensive ab initio study of hot carrier dynamics governed by electron-phonon scattering at the h h -BN/graphene interface, using graphite (bulk), monolayer and bilayer graphene as benchmark materials.

title: Investigations on Speech Recognition Systems for Low-Resource Dialectal Arabic-English Code-Switching Speech
creator: Injy Hamed, Pavel Denisov, Chia-Yu Li, Mohamed Elmahdy, Slim Abdennadher, Ngoc Thang Vu
description: Abstract Code-switching (CS), defined as the mixing of languages in conversations, has become a worldwide phenomenon. The prevalence of CS has been recently met with a growing demand and interest to build CS ASR systems. In this paper, we present our work on code-switched Egyptian Arabic-English automatic speech recognition (ASR).

title: Edge Statistics for Lozenge Tilings of Polygons, II: Airy Line Ensemble
creator: Amol Aggarwal 1,2, Jiaoyang Huang 3
description: Abstract . We consider uniformly random lozenge tilings of simply connected polygons subject to a technical assumption on their limit shape. We show that the edge statistics around any point on the arctic boundary, that is not a cusp or tangency location, converge to the Airy line ensemble.

title: A multispecies pseudoadiabat for simulating condensable-rich exoplanet atmospheres
creator: R.J. Graham, Tim Lichtenberg, Ryan Boukrouche, Raymond T. Pierrehumbert
description: Abstract Central stages in the evolution of rocky, potentially habitable planets may play out under atmospheric conditions with a large inventory of non-dilute condensable components. Variations in condensate retention and accompanying changes in local lapse rate may substantially affect planetary climate and surface conditions, but there is currently no general theory to effectively describe such atmospheres.

title: Tight Guarantees for Static Threshold Policies in the Prophet Secretary Problem
creator: Nick Arnosti, Will Ma
description: Abstract In the prophet secretary problem, n n values are drawn independently from known distributions, and presented in a uniformly random order. A decision-maker must accept or reject each value when it is presented, and may accept at most k k values in total. The objective is to maximize the expected sum of accepted values.

title: Precision measurement of the Lamb shift in Muonium
creator: B. Ohayon, G. Janka, I. Cortinovis, Z. Burkley, L. de Sousa Borges, E. Depero, A. Golovizin, X. Ni, Z. Salman, A. Suter, C. Vigo, T. Prokscha, P. Crivelli, Mu-MASS collaboration
description: Abstract We report a new measurement of the n = 2 n=2 Lamb shift in Muonium using microwave spectroscopy. Our result of 1047.2 ​ ( 2.3 ) stat ​ ( 1.1 ) syst 1047.2(2.3)_{\textrm{stat}}(1.1)_{\textrm{syst}} MHz comprises an order of magnitude improvement upon the previous best measurement.

title: Lipschitz Continuity Guided Knowledge Distillation
creator: Yuzhang Shang, Bin Duan , Ziliang Zong, Liqiang Nie, Yan Yan
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yuzhang Shang, Bin Duan , Ziliang Zong, Liqiang Nie, Yan Yan. Knowledge distillation has become one of the most important model compression techniques by distilling knowledge from larger teacher networks to smaller student ones. Although great success has been achieved by prior distillation methods via delicately designing various types of knowledge, they overlook the functional properties of neural networks, which makes the process of applying those techniques to new tasks unreliable and non-trivial.

title: RetroGAN: A Cyclic Post-Specialization System for Improving Out-of-Knowledge and Rare Word Representations Thanks: Work done while at the MIT Media Lab
creator: Pedro Colon-Hernandez, Yida Xin, Henry Lieberman, Catherine Havasi, Cynthia Breazeal, Peter Chin
description: Abstract Retrofitting is a technique used to move word vectors closer together or further apart in their space to reflect their relationships in a Knowledge Base (KB). However, retrofitting only works on concepts that are present in that KB. RetroGAN uses a pair of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to learn a one-to-one mapping between concepts and their retrofitted counterparts.

title: Mischievous Nominal Constructions in Universal Dependencies
creator: Nathan Schneider, Amir Zeldes
description: Abstract While the highly multilingual Universal Dependencies (UD) project provides extensive guidelines for clausal structure as well as structure within canonical nominal phrases, a standard treatment is lacking for many “mischievous” nominal phenomena that break the mold. As a result, numerous inconsistencies within and across corpora can be found, even in languages with extensive UD treebanking work, such as English.

title: KO codes: Inventing Nonlinear Encoding and Decoding for Reliable Wireless Communication via Deep-learning
creator: Ashok Vardhan Makkuva, Xiyang Liu, Mohammad Vahid Jamali, Hessam Mahdavifar, Sewoong Oh, Pramod Viswanath
description: Abstract Landmark codes underpin reliable physical layer communication, e.g., Reed-Muller, BCH, Convolution, Turbo, LDPC and Polar codes: each is a linear code and represents a mathematical breakthrough. The impact on humanity is huge: each of these codes has been used in global wireless communication standards (satellite, WiFi, cellular).

title: On limits of betweenness relations
creator: David Bradley-Williams and John K. Truss
description: Abstract . We give a flexible method for constructing a wide variety of limits of betweenness relations. This unifies work of Adeleke, who constructed a Jordan group preserving a limit of betweenness relations, and Bhattacharjee and Macpherson who gave an alternative method using a Fraïssé-type construction. A key ingredient in their work is the notion of a tree of B-sets.

title: UNSUPERVISED LEARNING OF DEEP FEATURES FOR MUSIC SEGMENTATION
creator: Matthew C. McCallum
description: Abstract Music segmentation refers to the dual problem of identifying boundaries between, and labeling, distinct music segments, e.g., the chorus, verse, bridge etc. in popular music. The performance of a range of music segmentation algorithms has been shown to be dependent on the audio features chosen to represent the audio.

title: Learning to Discover Reflection Symmetry via Polar Matching Convolution
creator: Ahyun Seo, Woohyeon ShimMinsu ChoPohang University of Science and Technology (POSTECH), South Korea http://cvlab.postech.ac.kr/research/PMCNet
description: Abstract The task of reflection symmetry detection remains challenging due to significant variations and ambiguities of symmetry patterns in the wild. Furthermore, since the local regions are required to match in reflection for detecting a symmetry pattern, it is hard for standard convolutional networks, which are not equivariant to rotation and reflection, to learn the task.

title: Quantum stability of Proca-Nuevo
creator: Claudia de Rham, Lavinia Heisenberg, Ankip Kumar, and Jann Zosso
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Claudia de Rham, Lavinia Heisenberg, Ankip Kumar, and Jann Zosso. The construction of general derivative self-interactions for a massive Proca field relies on the well-known condition for constrained systems of having a degenerate Hessian. The nature of the existing constraints algebra will distinguish among different classes of interactions. Proca-Nuevo interactions enjoy a non–trivial constraint by mixing terms of various order whereas Generalized Proca interactions satisfy the degeneracy condition order by order for each individual Lagrangians.

title: Enhancing d d -wave superconductivity with nearest-neighbor attraction of extended Hubbard model
creator: Mi Jiang
description: Abstract Motivated by the recent discovery of the anomalously nearest-neighbor attraction arising from the electron-phonon coupling, we quantitatively investigate the enhancing effects of this additional attractive channel on the d d -wave SC based on dynamic cluster quantum Monte Carlo calculations of doped two-dimensional extended Hubbard model with nearest-neighbor attraction − V -V .

title: WIMP Dark Matter Hidden behind its Companion
creator: Jun Guo, Zhaofeng Kang, Peng Zhang
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jun Guo, Zhaofeng Kang, Peng Zhang. The WIMP dark matter (DM) hypothesis now is in an awkward position, owing to the stronger and stronger exclusion from DM direct detection. In this article we design a mechanism to evade this constraint. DM has a companion, and they are both charged under the DM protecting symmetry G G ; they admit the trilinear coupling DM-DM-companion, so the latter provides a portal to the standard model (SM) via, for instance, the coupling to Higgs doublet.

title: Digging into Uncertainty in Self-supervised Multi-view Stereo
creator: Hongbin Xu, Zhipeng Zhou, Yali Wang, Wenxiong Kang, Baigui Sun, Hao Li, Yu Qiao
description: Abstract Self-supervised Multi-view stereo (MVS) with a pretext task of image reconstruction has achieved significant progress recently. However, previous methods are built upon intuitions, lacking comprehensive explanations about the effectiveness of the pretext task in self-supervised MVS. To this end, we propose to estimate epistemic uncertainty in self-supervised MVS, accounting for what the model ignores.

title: Neural homogenization and the physics-informed neural network for the multiscale problems
creator: Wing Tat Leung, Guang Lin, Zecheng Zhang
description: Abstract Physics-informed neural network (PINN) is a data-driven approach to solve equations. It is successful in many applications; however, the accuracy of the PINN is not satisfactory when it is used to solve multiscale equations. Homogenization is a way of approximating a multiscale equation by a homogenized equation without multiscale property; it includes solving cell problems and the homogenized equation.

title: Font Completion and Manipulation by Cycling Between Multi-Modality Representations
creator: Ye Yuan, Wuyang Chen, Zhaowen Wang, Matthew Fisher, Zhifei Zhang, Zhangyang Wang, Hailin Jin
description: Abstract Generating font glyphs of consistent style from one or a few reference glyphs, i.e., font completion, is an important task in topographical design. As the problem is more well-defined than general image style transfer tasks, thus it has received interest from both vision and machine learning communities. Existing approaches address this problem as a direct image-to-image translation task.

title: Kinetic construction of the high-beta anisotropic-pressure equilibrium in the magnetosphere
creator: H. Aibara, Z. Yoshida, K. Shirahata
description: Abstract A theoretical model of the high-beta equilibrium of magnetospheric plasma was constructed by consistently connecting the (anisotropic pressure) Grad–Shafranov equation and the Vlasov equation. The Grad–Shafranov equation was used to determine the axisymmetric magnetic field for a given magnetization current corresponding to a pressure tensor.

title: Correlation of Gravitational Wave Background Noises and Statistical Loss for Angular Averaged Sensitivity Curves
creator: Naoki Seto
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Naoki Seto. Gravitational wave backgrounds generate correlated noises to separated detectors. This correlation can induce statistical losses to actual detector networks, compared with idealized noise-independent networks. Assuming that the backgrounds are isotropic, we examine the statistical losses specifically for the angular averaged sensitivity curves, and derive simple expressions that depend on the overlap reduction functions and the strength of the background noises relative to the instrumental noises.

title: On the analyticity of WLUD ∞ functions of one variable and WLUD ∞ functions of several variables in a complete non-Archimedean valued field Thanks: This research was funded by the Natural Sciences and Engineering Council of Canada (NSERC, Grant # RGPIN/4965-2017)
creator: Khodr Shamseddine
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Khodr Shamseddine. Let 𝒩 \mathcal{N} be a non-Archimedean ordered field extension of the real numbers that is real closed and Cauchy complete in the topology induced by the order, and whose Hahn group is Archimedean. In this paper, we first review the properties of weakly locally uniformly differentiable (WLUD) functions, k k times weakly locally uniformly differentiable (WLUD k ) functions, and WLUD ∞ functions [ 1 , 12 ] at a point or on an open subset of 𝒩 \mathcal{N} .

title: Approaching the Basis Set Limit in Gaussian-Orbital-Based Periodic Calculations with Transferability: Performance of Pure Density Functionals for Simple Semiconductors
creator: Joonho Lee, Xintian Feng, Leonardo A. Cunha, Jérôme F. Gonthier, Evgeny Epifanovsky, Martin Head-Gordon
description: Abstract Simulating solids with quantum chemistry methods and Gaussian-type orbitals (GTOs) has been gaining popularity. Nonetheless, there are few systematic studies that assess the basis set incompleteness error (BSIE) in these GTO-based simulations over a variety of solids. In this work, we report a GTO-based implementation for solids, and apply it to address the basis set convergence issue.

title: Homological properties of extensions of algebras
creator: Kostiantyn Iusenko, John William MacQuarrie
description: Abstract We consider a class of extensions of associative algebras, which we refer to as “strongly proj-bounded extensions”. We prove that the finiteness of the left global dimension and the support of the Hochschild homology is preserved by strongly proj-bounded extensions, generalizing results of Cibils, Lanzillota, Marcos and Solotar.

title: A local C 2 C^{2} Hermite interpolation scheme with PH quintic splines for 3D data streams
creator: Carlotta Giannelli, Lorenzo Sacco, Alessandra Sestini
description: Abstract The construction of smooth spatial paths with Pythagorean-hodograph (PH) quintic spline biarcs is proposed. To facilitate real-time computations of C 2 C^{2} PH quintic splines, an efficient local data stream interpolation algorithm is introduced. Each spline segment interpolates second and first order Hermite data at the initial and final end-point, respectively.

title: Continuous Differentiability of the Value Function of Semilinear Parabolic Infinite Time Horizon Optimal Control Problems on L 2 ​ ( Ω ) L^{2}(\Omega) under Control Constraints Thanks: The authors were supported by the ERC advanced grant 668998 (OCLOC) under the EU’s H2020 research program.
creator: Karl Kunisch, Buddhika Priyasad
description: Abstract An abstract framework guaranteeing the local continuous differentiability of the value function associated with optimal stabilization problems subject to abstract semilinear parabolic equations subject to a norm constraint on the controls is established. It guarantees that the value function satisfies the associated Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation in the classical sense.

title: What’s in a name? Quantifying the interplay between the Definition, Orientation, and Shape of Ultra-diffuse Galaxies Using the Romulus Simulations Journal: ApJ
creator: Jordan D. Van Nest, F. Munshi, A.C. Wright, M. Tremmel, A.M. Brooks, D. Nagai, T. Quinn
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jordan D. Van Nest, F. Munshi, A.C. Wright, M. Tremmel, A.M. Brooks, D. Nagai, T. Quinn. We explore populations of ultra-diffuse galaxies (UDGs) in isolated, satellite, and cluster environments using the R omulus 25 and R omulus C simulations, including how the populations vary with UDG definition and viewing orientation.

title: The gamma-ray emission from 3HWC J1928+178
description: Abstract The gamma-ray source 3HWC J1928+178, discovered by HAWC, is coincident with the 82 kyr pulsar PSR J1928+1746, located 4 kpc away. It has not been reported by any Imaging atmospheric Cherenkov Telescope (IACT), until the recent detection of emission from this region by H.E.S.S., using an analysis adapted to extended sources.

title: X2Teeth: 3D Teeth Reconstruction from a Single Panoramic Radiograph
creator: Yuan Liang, Weinan Song, Jiawei Yang, Liang Qiu, Kun Wang, Lei He
description: Abstract 3D teeth reconstruction from X-ray is important for dental diagnosis and many clinical operations. However, no existing work has explored the reconstruction of teeth for a whole cavity from a single panoramic radiograph. Different from single object reconstruction from photos, this task has the unique challenge of constructing multiple objects at high resolutions.

title: Almost everywhere convergence of Fourier series on compact connected Lie groups
creator: David Grow and Donnie Myers
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by David Grow and Donnie Myers. We consider the open problem: Does every square-integrable function f f on a compact, connected Lie group G G have an almost everywhere convergent Fourier series? We prove a general theorem from which it follows that if the integral modulus of continuity of f f is O ⁡ ( t α ) O(t^{\alpha}) for some α > 0 \alpha>0 then the Fourier series of f f converges almost everywhere on G G .

title: Atomic data and the density structures of planetary nebulae 2015 Atomic data and the density structures of planetary nebulae – References
creator: Leticia Juan de Dios, Mónica Rodríguez
description: Abstract We study the density structures of planetary nebulae implied by four diagnostics that sample different regions within the nebulae: [ S ii ] λ ​ 6716 / λ ​ 6731 \lambda 6716/\lambda 6731 , [ O ii ] λ ​ 3726 / λ ​ 3729 \lambda 3726/\lambda 3729 , [ Cl iii ] λ ​ 5518 / λ ​

title: On the Chromatic Vertex Stability Number of Graphs
creator: Saieed Akbari, Arash Beikmohammadi, Sandi Klavžar, Nazanin Movarraei
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Saieed Akbari, Arash Beikmohammadi, Sandi Klavžar, Nazanin Movarraei. The chromatic vertex (resp. edge) stability number vs χ ​ ( G ) {\rm vs}_{\chi}(G) (resp. es χ ​ ( G ) {\rm es}_{\chi}(G) ) of a graph G G is the minimum number of vertices (resp. edges) whose deletion results in a graph H H with χ ⁡ ( H ) = χ ⁡ ( G ) − 1 \chi(H)=\chi(G)-1 .

title: Lithium Evolution of Giant Stars Observed by LAMOST and Kepler
creator: Jinghua Zhang, Jian-Rong Shi, Hong-Liang Yan, Yaguang Li, Qi Gao, Chun-Qian Li, Xianfei Zhang, Shuai Liu, Shaolan Bi, Gang Zhao, Yan Li
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jinghua Zhang, Jian-Rong Shi, Hong-Liang Yan, Yaguang Li, Qi Gao, Chun-Qian Li, Xianfei Zhang, Shuai Liu, Shaolan Bi, Gang Zhao, Yan Li. Mapping lithium evolution for evolved stars will provide restrictions and constraints on the fundamental stellar interior physical processes, which further shed light on our understanding of the theory of stellar structure and evolution.

title: Production of the T c ​ c + T^{+}_{cc} state in the γ ​ p → D + ​ T ¯ c ​ c − ​ Λ c + \gamma{}p\to{}D^{+}\bar{T}^{-}_{cc}\Lambda_{c}^{+} reaction
creator: Yin Huang 1, Hong Qiang Zhu 2, Li-Sheng Geng 3, Rong Wang 4,5
description: Abstract Stimulated by the recent LHCb observation of a new exotic charged structure T c ​ c + T^{+}_{cc} , we propose to use the central diffractive mechanism existing in the γ ​ p → D + ​ T ¯ c ​ c − ​ Λ c + \gamma{}p\to{}D^{+}\bar{T}^{-}_{cc}\Lambda_{c}^{+} ( T ¯ c ​ c \bar{T}_{cc} is antiparticle of T

title: Quantum Alternating Operator Ansatz (QAOA) Phase Diagrams and Applications for Quantum Chemistry
creator: Vladimir Kremenetski, Tad Hogg, Stuart Hadfield, Stephen J. Cotton, Norm M. Tubman
description: Abstract We adapt the Quantum Alternating Operator Ansatz (QAOA) to find ground states in quantum chemistry problems and empirically evaluate our protocol on several molecules. These simulations show robust qualitative behavior for QAOA as a function of the number of steps and size of the parameters.

title: Data-driven Small-signal Modeling for Converter-based Power Systems Journal: Sustainable Energy, Grids and Networks
creator: Francesca Rossi, Eduardo Prieto-Araujo, Marc Cheah-Mane, Oriol Gomis-Bellmunt
description: Abstract This article details a complete procedure to derive a data-driven small-signal-based model useful to perform converter-based power system related studies. To compute the model, Decision Tree (DT) regression, both using single DT and ensemble DT, and Spline regression have been employed and their performances have been compared, in terms of accuracy, training and computing time.

title: Proposed Negative Thermal Expansion in Honeycomb-Lattice Antiferromagnets
creator: Yuto Uwabo, Masahito Mochizuki
description: Abstract We theoretically propose possible magnetism-induced negative thermal expansion in honeycomb-lattice antiferromagnets with edge-sharing networks of M ​ X 6 MX_{6} octahedra where M M and X X are transition-metal and ligand ions, respectively. In this crystal structure, the nearest-neighbor exchange interaction is composed of two competing contributions, i.e.

title: An inverse problem for the porous medium equation with partial data and a possibly singular absorption term
creator: Cătălin I. Cârstea, Tuhin Ghosh, Gunther Uhlmann
description: Abstract In this paper we prove uniqueness in the inverse boundary value problem for the three coefficient functions in the porous medium equation with an absorption term ϵ ∂ t u − ∇ ⋅ ( γ ∇ u m ) + λ u q = 0 \epsilon\partial_{t}u-\nabla\cdot(\gamma\nabla u^{m})+\lambda u^{q}=0 , with m > 1 m>1 , m − 1 <

title: Shatter : An Efficient Transformer Encoder with Single-Headed Self-Attention and Relative Sequence Partitioning
creator: Ran Tian, Joshua Maynez, Ankur P. Parikh
description: Abstract The highly popular Transformer architecture, based on self-attention, is the foundation of large pretrained models such as BERT, that have become an enduring paradigm in NLP. While powerful, the computational resources and time required to pretrain such models can be prohibitive.

title: QUANTUM NON-GAUSSIANITY FROM AN INDEFNITE CAUSAL ORDER OF GAUSSIAN OPERATIONS
creator: SEID KOUDIA, ABDELHAKIM GHARBI
description: Abstract Quantum Non-Gaussian states are considered as a useful resource for many tasks in quantum information processing, from quantum metrology and quantum sensing to quantum communication and quantum key distribution. Another useful tool that is growing attention is the newly constructed quantum switch.

title: A Further Improvement on Approximating TTP-2
creator: Jingyang Zhao, Mingyu Xiao
description: Abstract The Traveling Tournament Problem (TTP) is a hard but interesting sports scheduling problem inspired by Major League Baseball, which is to design a double round-robin schedule such that each pair of teams plays one game in each other’s home venue, minimizing the total distance traveled by all n n teams ( n n is even).

title: Relativistic hybrid stars in light of the NICER PSR J0740+6620 radius measurement
creator: Jia Jie Li, Armen Sedrakian, Mark Alford
description: Abstract We explore the implications of the recent radius determination of PSR J0740+6620 by the NICER experiment combined with the neutron skin measurement by the PREX-II experiment and the associated inference of the slope of symmetry energy, for the structure of hybrid stars with a strong first-order phase transition from nucleonic to quark matter.

title: Private Multi-Task Learning: Formulation and Applications to Federated Learning
creator: Shengyuan Hu shengyuanhu@cmu.edu, Zhiwei Steven Wu zstevenwu@cmu.edu, Virginia Smith smithv@cmu.edu
description: Abstract Many problems in machine learning rely on multi-task learning (MTL) , in which the goal is to solve multiple related machine learning tasks simultaneously. MTL is particularly relevant for privacy-sensitive applications in areas such as healthcare, finance, and IoT computing, where sensitive data from multiple, varied sources are shared for the purpose of learning.

title: SHIFT15M: Fashion-specific dataset for set-to-set matching with several distribution shifts
creator: Masanari Kimura, Takuma Nakamura, Yuki Saito
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Masanari Kimura, Takuma Nakamura, Yuki Saito. This paper addresses the problem of set-to-set matching, which involves matching two different sets of items based on some criteria, especially in the case of high-dimensional items like images. Although neural networks have been applied to solve this problem, most machine learning-based approaches assume that the training and test data follow the same distribution, which is not always true in real-world scenarios.

title: InSE-NET: A Perceptually Coded Audio Quality Model based on CNN
description: Abstract Automatic coded audio quality assessment is an important task whose progress is hampered by the scarcity of human annotations, poor generalization to unseen codecs, bitrates, content-types, and a lack of flexibility of existing approaches. One of the typical human-perception-related metrics, ViSQOL v3 (ViV3), has been proven to provide a high correlation to the quality scores rated by humans.

title: Accurate electron beam phase-space theory for ionisation injection schemes driven by laser pulses
creator: Paolo Tomassini 1 , Francesco Massimo 2 , Luca Labate 1,3 and Leonida A. Gizzi 1,3
description: Abstract After the introduction of the ionization-injection scheme in Laser Wake Field Acceleration and of related high-quality electron beam generation methods as two-color or the Resonant Multi Pulse Ionization injection, the theory of thermal emittance by C. Schroeder et al . has been used to predict the beam normalised emittance obtainable with those schemes.

title: Velocity difference of ions and neutrals in solar prominences
creator: E. Wiehr, G. Stellmacher, H. Balthasar, and M. Bianda
description: Abstract Marked velocity excesses of ions relative to neutrals are obtained from two time series of the neighboring emission lines He i 5015 Å and Fe ii 5018 Å in a quiescent prominence. Their Doppler shifts show time variations of quasi-periodic character where the ions are faster than the neutrals 1.

title: NEREL: A Russian Dataset with Nested Named Entities, Relations and Events
creator: Natalia Loukachevitch, Ekaterina Artemova, Tatiana Batura, Pavel Braslavski, Ilia Denisov, Vladimir Ivanov, Suresh Manandhar, Alexander Pugachev, Elena Tutubalina
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Natalia Loukachevitch, Ekaterina Artemova, Tatiana Batura, Pavel Braslavski, Ilia Denisov, Vladimir Ivanov, Suresh Manandhar, Alexander Pugachev, Elena Tutubalina. In this paper, we present NEREL, a Russian dataset for named entity recognition and relation extraction. NEREL is significantly larger than existing Russian datasets: to date it contains 56K annotated named entities and 39K annotated relations. Its important difference from previous datasets is annotation of nested named entities, as well as relations within nested entities and at the discourse level.

title: Piecewise monotone estimation in one-parameter exponential family
creator: Takeru Matsuda, Yuto Miyatake
description: Abstract The problem of estimating a piecewise monotone sequence of normal means is called the nearly isotonic regression. For this problem, an efficient algorithm has been devised by modifying the pool adjacent violators algorithm (PAVA). In this study, we investigate estimation of a piecewise monotone parameter sequence for general one-parameter exponential families such as binomial, Poisson and chi-square.

title: Theory of wakefields excited by an off–axis drive bunch in a plasma–dielectric waveguide
creator: K.V. Galaydych, G.V. Sotnikov, I.N. Onishchenko
description: Abstract A linear theory of wakefield excitation by a drive electron bunch in a plasma–dielectric accelerating structure has been constructed for the case of off–axis bunch injection. The structure under investigation is a round dielectric–loaded metal waveguide with a channel for charged particles, filled with homogeneous cold plasma.

title: Merger Histories and Environments of Dwarf AGN in IllustrisTNG
creator: Mikkel Theiss Kristensen, Kevin Pimbblet, Brad Gibson, Samantha Penny, Sophie Koudmani
description: Abstract The relationship between active galactic nuclei activity and environment has been long discussed, but it is unclear if these relations extend into the dwarf galaxy mass regime – in part due to the limits in both observations and simulations.

title: Sheaves of noncommutative smooth and holomorphic functions associated with the non-Abelian two-dimensional Lie algebra Thanks: This work was supported by the Russian Foundation for Basic Research under grant 19-01-00447.
creator: O. Yu. Aristov
description: Abstract . Dosi and, quite recently, the author showed that, on the character space of a nilpotent Lie algebra, there exists a sheaf of Fréchet–Arens–Michael algebras (of noncommutative holomorphic functions in the complex case and of noncommutative smooth functions in the real case).

title: An outer totalistic weakly universal cellular automaton in the dodecagrid with four states
creator: Maurice Margenstern
description: Abstract In this paper, we prove that there is an outer totalistic weakly universal cellular automaton in the dodecagrid, the tessellation { 5 , 3 , 4 } \{5,3,4\} of the hyperbolic 3 ​ D 3D space, with four states. It is the first result in such a context.

title: Enhancing Spin Polarization Using Ultrafast Angular Streaking
creator: G. S. J. Armstrong, D. D. A. Clarke, J. Benda, J. Wragg, A. C. Brown, H. W. van der Hart
description: Abstract Through solution of the multielectron, semi-relativistic, time-dependent Schrödinger equation, we show that angular streaking produces strongly spin-polarized electrons in a noble gas. The degree of spin polarization increases with the Keldysh parameter, so that angular streaking — ordinarily applied to investigate tunneling — may be repurposed to generate strongly spin-polarized electron bunches.

title: Helmholtz : A Verifier for Tezos Smart Contracts Based on Refinement Types
creator: Yuki Nishida, Hiromasa Saito, Ran Chen, Akira Kawata, Jun Furuse, Kohei Suenaga, Atsushi Igarashi
description: Abstract A smart contract is a program executed on a blockchain, based on which many cryptocurrencies are implemented, and is being used for automating transactions. Due to the large amount of money that smart contracts deal with, there is a surging demand for a method that can statically and formally verify them.

title: Tune It or Don’t Use It: Benchmarking Data-Efficient Image Classification
creator: Lorenzo Brigato, Björn Barz, Luca Iocchi, Joachim Denzler
description: Abstract Data-efficient image classification using deep neural networks in settings, where only small amounts of labeled data are available, has been an active research area in the recent past. However, an objective comparison between published methods is difficult, since existing works use different datasets for evaluation and often compare against untuned baselines with default hyper-parameters.

title: Dynamics of thermalization of two tunnel-coupled one-dimensional quasicondensates
creator: F. A. Bayocboc, Jr, M. J. Davis, K. V. Kheruntsyan
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by F. A. Bayocboc, Jr, M. J. Davis, K. V. Kheruntsyan. We study the non-equilibrium dynamics of two tunnel-coupled one-dimensional quasicondensates following a quench of the coupling strength from zero to a fixed finite value. More specifically, starting from two independent quasicondensates in thermal equilibrium, with initial temperature and chemical potential imbalance, we suddenly switch on the tunnel-coupling and analyse the post-quench equilibration in terms of particle number and energy imbalances.

title: Aleatoric Description Logic for Probabilistic Reasoning (Long Version)
creator: Tim French, Thomas Smoker
description: Abstract Description logics are a powerful tool for describing ontological knowledge bases. That is, they give a factual account of the world in terms of individuals, concepts and relations. In the presence of uncertainty, such factual accounts are not feasible, and a subjective or epistemic approach is required.

title: Neuron-level Interpretation of Deep NLP Models: A Survey Thanks: The work was done while the author was at QCRI
creator: Hassan Sajjad Nadir Durrani Fahim Dalvi hsajjad@dal.ca, {ndurrani, faimaduddin}@hbku.edu.qa
description: Abstract The proliferation of deep neural networks in various domains has seen an increased need for interpretability of these models. Preliminary work done along this line and papers that surveyed such, are focused on high-level representation analysis. However, a recent branch of work has concentrated on interpretability at a more granular level of analyzing neurons within these models.

title: DuTrust: A Sentiment Analysis Dataset for Trustworthiness Evaluation
creator: Lijie Wang, Hao Liu, Shuyuan Peng, Hongxuan Tang, Xinyan Xiao, Ying Chen, Hua Wu, Haifeng WangBaidu Inc., Beijing, China {wanglijie,liuhao24,pengshuyuan,tanghongxuan,xiaoxinyan,chenying04,hua_wu,wanghaifeng}@baidu.com
description: Abstract While deep learning models have greatly improved the performance of most artificial intelligence tasks, they are often criticized to be untrustworthy due to the black-box problem. Consequently, many works have been proposed to study the trustworthiness of deep learning.

title: BDD-Based Algorithm for SCC Decomposition of Edge-Coloured Graphs
creator: Nikola Beneš, Luboš Brim, Samuel Pastva, David Šafránek
description: Abstract . Edge-coloured directed graphs provide an essential structure for modelling and analysis of complex systems arising in many scientific disciplines (e.g. feature-oriented systems, gene regulatory networks, etc.). One of the fundamental problems for edge-coloured graphs is the detection of strongly connected components, or SCCs.

title: Lower bounds for moments of the derivative of the Riemann zeta function
creator: Peng Gao
description: Abstract . We establish in this paper sharp lower bounds for the 2 ​ k 2k -th moment of the derivative of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line for all real k ≥ 0 k\geq 0 . Mathematics Subject Classification (2010) : 11M06 Keywords : lower bounds, moments, derivative, Riemman zeta function 1.

title: Multi-armed quantum bandits: Exploration versus exploitation when learning properties of quantum states
creator: Josep Lumbreras, Erkka Haapasalo, Marco Tomamichel
description: Abstract We initiate the study of tradeoffs between exploration and exploitation in online learning of properties of quantum states. Given sequential oracle access to an unknown quantum state, in each round, we are tasked to choose an observable from a set of actions aiming to maximize its expectation value on the state (the reward).

title: Probing many-body systems near spectral degeneracies
creator: K. Ziegler
description: Abstract The diagonal elements of the time correlation matrix are used to probe closed quantum systems that are measured at random times. This enables us to extract two distinct parts of the quantum evolution, a recurrent part and an exponentially decaying part. This separation is strongly affected when spectral degeneracies occur, for instance, in the presence of spontaneous symmetry breaking.

title: Positive Solution for a Hadamard Fractional Singular Boundary Value Problem of Order μ ∈ ( 2 , 3 ) \mu\in(2,\,3)
creator: Naseer Ahmad Asif
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Naseer Ahmad Asif. In this article, we establish the existence of positive solution for the following Hadamard fractional singular boundary value problem D μ a + H ​ x ​ ( t ) + f ⁡ ( t , x ⁡ ( t ) ) \displaystyle{}^{H}D_{a^{+}}^{\,\mu}x(t)+f(t,x(t)) = 0 , t ∈ ( a , b ) , 0 < a < b < ∞ , 2 < μ < 3 , \displaystyle=0,\hskip 11.38092ptt\in(a,\,b),\hskip 11.38092pt0<a<b<\infty,\hskip 11.38092pt2<\mu<3, x ⁡ ( a ) = a ​ x

title: Solving the puzzle of high temperature light (anti)-nuclei production in ultra-relativistic heavy ion collisions
creator: Tim Neidig, Kai Gallmeister, Carsten Greiner, Marcus Bleicher, Volodymyr Vovchenko
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Tim Neidig, Kai Gallmeister, Carsten Greiner, Marcus Bleicher, Volodymyr Vovchenko. The creation of loosely bound objects in heavy ion collisions, e.g. light clusters, near the phase transition temperature ( T ch ≈ 155 ​ MeV T_{\rm ch}\approx 155\,{\rm MeV} ) has been a puzzling observation that seems to be at odds with Big Bang nucleosynthesis suggesting that deuterons and other clusters are formed only below a temperature T ≈ 0.1 − 1 ​ MeV T\approx 0.1-1\,{\rm MeV} .

title: Probabilistic Verification for Reliability of a Two-by-Two Network-on-Chip System
creator: Riley Roberts, Benjamin Lewis, Arnd Hartmanns, Prabal Basu, Sanghamitra Roy, Koushik Chakraborty, Zhen Zhang
description: Abstract Modern network-on-chip (NoC) systems face reliability issues due to process and environmental variations. The power supply noise (PSN) in the power delivery network of a NoC plays a key role in determining reliability. PSN leads to voltage droop, which can cause timing errors in the NoC. This paper makes a novel contribution towards formally analyzing PSN in NoC systems.

title: NOMA Assisted Multi-MEC Offloading for IoVT Networks
creator: Fengqian Guo, Hancheng Lu, Bo Li, Dingxuan Li, Chang Wen Chen
description: Abstract Abstract Nowadays, Internet of Video Things (IoVT) grows rapidly in terms of quantity and computation demands. In spite of the higher local computation capability on visual processing compared with conventional Internet of Things devices, IoVT devices need to offload partial visual processing tasks to the mobile edge computing (MEC) server wirelessly due to its larger computation demands.

title: THE LIMIT AS p → ∞ p\rightarrow\infty FOR THE p − p- LAPLACIAN EQUATION WITH DYNAMICAL BOUNDARY CONDITIONS
creator: Eylem Öztürk, Julio D. Rossi
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Eylem Öztürk, Julio D. Rossi. In this paper we study the limit as p → ∞ p\to\infty in the evolution problem driven by the p − p- Laplacian with dynamical boundary conditions. We prove that the natural energy functional associated with this problem converges to a limit in the sense of Mosco convergence and as a consequence we obtain convergence of the solutions to the evolution problems.

title: Non-linear elasticity, yielding and entropy in amorphous solids
creator: Deng Pan, Teng Ji, Matteo Baggioli, Li Li, Yuliang Jin
description: Abstract The holographic duality has proven successful in linking seemingly unrelated problems in physics. Recently, intriguing correspondences between the physics of soft matter and gravity are emerging, including strong similarities between the rheology of amorphous solids, effective field theories for elasticity and the physics of black holes. However, direct comparisons between theoretical predictions and experimental/simulation observations remain limited.

title: Soft quantum waveguides in three dimensions
creator: Pavel Exner
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Pavel Exner. We discuss a three-dimensional soft quantum waveguide, in other words, Schrödinger operator in ℝ 3 \mathbb{R}^{3} with an attractive potential supported by an infinite tube and keeping its transverse profile fixed. We show that if the tube is asymptotically straight, the distance between its ends is unbounded, and its twist satisfies the so-called Tang condition, the esential spectrum is not affected by smooth bends.

title: On the Smallest Non-trivial Action of SAut ⁡ ( F n ) \operatorname{SAut}(F_{n}) for Small n n
creator: Reemon Spector
description: Abstract Abstract. In this paper we investigate actions of \operatorname{SAut}(F_{n}) , the unique index 2 subgroup of \operatorname{Aut}(F_{n}) , on small sets, improving upon results by Baumeister–Kielak–Pierro for several small values of n . Using a computational approach for n\geqslant 5 , we show that every action of \operatorname{SAut}(F_{n}) on a set containing fewer than 18 elements is trivial.

title: New results for the random nearest neighbor tree
creator: Lyuben Lichev, Dieter Mitsche
description: Abstract In this paper, we study the online nearest neighbor random tree in dimension d ∈ ℕ d\in\mathbb{N} (called d d -NN tree for short) defined as follows. We fix the torus 𝕋 n d \mathbb{T}^{d}_{n} of dimension d d and area n n and equip it with the metric inherited from the Euclidean metric in ℝ d \mathbb{R}^{d} .

title: Gravitational radiation pulses from Extreme-Mass-Ratio-Inspiral system with a supermassive boson star
creator: Yu-Peng Zhang 1, 2 , Yan-Bo Zeng 1, 2 , Yong-Qiang Wang 1, 2 , Shao-Wen Wei 1, 2 , Pau Amaro Seoane 3, 4, 5, 6 , Yu-Xiao Liu 1, 2
description: Abstract Future space-borne gravitational-wave detectors will observe the gravitational waves in the milli-Hz. Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals with central supermassive black holes are very important sources that could provide the information of the vicinity of black holes. The event horizon separates the inner region of a black hole and there is nothing that can escape from this region.

title: DQLEL: Deep Q-Learning for Energy-Optimized LoS/NLoS UWB Node Selection
creator: Zohreh Hajiakhondi-Meybodi, Arash Mohammadi, Ming Hou, and Konstantinos N. Plataniotis
description: Abstract Recent advancements in Internet of Things (IoTs) have brought about a surge of interest in indoor positioning for the purpose of providing reliable, accurate, and energy-efficient indoor navigation/localization systems. Ultra Wide Band (UWB) technology has been emerged as a potential candidate to satisfy the aforementioned requirements.

title: Semiorthogonal decomposition via categorical action
creator: You-Hung Hsu
description: Abstract . We show that the categorical action of the shifted q = 0 q=0 affine algebra can be used to construct semiorthogonal decomposition on the weight categories. In particular, this construction recovers Kapranov’s exceptional collection when the weight categories are the derived categories of coherent sheaves on Grassmannians and n n -step partial flag varieties.

title: Stochastic synchronization induced by noise
creator: Yunxiang Song, Thomas A. Witten
description: Abstract Random perturbations applied in tandem to an ensemble of oscillating objects can synchronize their motion. We study multiple copies of an arbitrary dynamical system in a stable limit cycle, described via a standard phase reduction picture. The copies differ only in their arbitrary phases ϕ \phi .

title: Hessian heat kernel estimates and Calderón-Zygmund inequalities on complete Riemannian manifolds 0 0 footnotetext: * Corresponding author2010 Mathematics Subject Classification . Primary: 35K08; Secondary: 35J10, 35J30, 47G40. Key words and phrases . Brownian motion, Heat semigroup, Heat kernel, Bis
creator: Jun Cao, Li-Juan Cheng*, Anton Thalmaier
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jun Cao, Li-Juan Cheng*, Anton Thalmaier. We address some fundamental questions about geometric analysis on Riemannian manifolds. The L p L^{p} -Calderón-Zygmund inequality is one of the cornerstones in the regularity theory of elliptic equations, and it has been asked under which geometric conditions it holds for a reasonable class of non-compact Riemannian manifolds, and to what extent assumptions on the derivative of curvature and on the injectivity radius of the manifold are necessary.

title: A Dynamic Game Approach to Designing Secure Interdependent IoT-Enabled Infrastructure Network
creator: Juntao Chen, Corinne Touati, Quanyan Zhu
description: Abstract The emerging Internet of Things (IoT) applications that leverage ubiquitous connectivity and big data are facilitating the realization of smart everything initiatives. IoT-enabled infrastructures have naturally a multi-layer system architecture with an overlaid or underlaid device network and its coexisting infrastructure network.

title: Hyperbolic Basis Functions for Time-Transient Analysis of Eddy Currents in Conductive and Magnetic Thin Sheets
creator: Bruno de Sousa Alves 1 , Ruth V. Sabariego 2 , Marc Laforest 1 , and Frédéric Sirois 1
description: Abstract This paper presents a new time-domain finite-element approach for modelling thin sheets with hyperbolic basis functions derived from the well-known steady-state solution of the linear flux diffusion equation. The combination of solutions at different operating frequencies permits the representation of the time-evolution of field quantities in the magnetic field formulation.

title: High Performance GPU Code Generation for Matrix-Matrix Multiplication using MLIR: Some Early Results
creator: Navdeep Katel, Vivek Khandelwal, Uday Bondhugula
description: Abstract This report presents some early results on code generation targeting tensor cores on NVIDIA GPUs using the MLIR compiler infrastructure. The state-of-the-art in high-performance deep learning today is primarily driven by highly tuned libraries. These libraries are often hand-optimized and tuned by expert programmers using low-level abstractions with significant effort.

title: Reachability Is NP-Complete Even for the Simplest Neural Networks
creator: Marco Sälzer, Martin Lange
description: Abstract We investigate the complexity of the reachability problem for (deep) neural networks: does it compute valid output given some valid input? It was recently claimed that the problem is NP-complete for general neural networks and conjunctive input/output specifications. We repair some flaws in the original upper and lower bound proofs.

title: PTRAIL - A python package for parallel trajectory data preprocessing Journal: SoftwareX
creator: Salman Haidri, Yaksh J. Haranwala, Vania Bogorny, Chiara Renso, Vinicius Prado da Fonseca, Amilcar Soares
description: Abstract Trajectory data represent a trace of an object that changes its position in space over time. This kind of data is complex to handle and analyze, since it is generally produced in huge quantities, often prone to errors generated by the geolocation device, human mishandling, or area coverage limitation.

title: An automated near-real time computational method for induction and treatment of scar-related ventricular tachycardias
creator: Fernando O. Campos, Aurel Neic, Caroline Mendonca Costa, John Whitaker, Mark O’Neill, Reza Razavi, Christopher A. Rinaldi, Daniel Scherr, Steven A. Niederer, Gernot Plank, Martin J. Bishop
description: Abstract Catheter ablation is currently the only curative treatment for scar-related ventricular tachycardias (VTs). However, not only are ablation procedures long, with relatively high risk, but success rates are punitively low, with frequent VT recurrence. Personalized in-silico approaches have the opportunity to address these limitations.

title: Green’s function approach to the Bose-Hubbard model with disorder
creator: R S Souza, Axel Pelster, F E A dos Santos
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by R S Souza, Axel Pelster, F E A dos Santos. We analyse the distinction between the three different ground states presented by a system of spinless bosons with short-range interactions submitted to a random potential using the disordered Bose-Hubbard model. The criteria for identifying the superfluid, the Mott-insulator, and the Bose-glass phases at finite temperatures are discussed for small values of the kinetic energy associated with the tunnelling of particles between potential wells.

title: Geometrical aspect of susceptibility critical exponent
creator: Q. H. Liu
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Q. H. Liu. Critical exponent γ ⪰ 1.1 \gamma\succeq 1.1 characterizes behavior of the mechanical susceptibility of a real fluid when temperature approaches the critical one. It results in zero Gaussian curvature of the local shape of the critical point on the thermodynamic equation of state surface, which imposes a new constraint upon the construction of the potential equation of state of the real fluid from the empirical data.

title: Identification of novel organic polar materials: A study combining importance sampling with machine learning
creator: Ayana Ghosh, Dennis P. Trujillo, Subhashis Hazarika, Elizabeth Schiesser, M. J. Swamynathan, Saurabh Ghosh, Jian-Xin Zhu, Serge Nakhmanson
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Ayana Ghosh, Dennis P. Trujillo, Subhashis Hazarika, Elizabeth Schiesser, M. J. Swamynathan, Saurabh Ghosh, Jian-Xin Zhu, Serge Nakhmanson. Recent advances in the synthesis of polar molecular materials have produced practical alternatives to ferroelectric ceramics, opening up exciting new avenues for their incorporation into modern electronic devices.

title: Enhancement of electromagnetically induced transparency based Rydberg-atom electrometry through population repumping
creator: Nikunjkumar Prajapati, Amy K. Robinson, Samuel Berweger, Matthew T. Simons, Alexandra B. Artusio-Glimpse, Christopher L. Holloway
description: Abstract We demonstrate improved sensitivity of Rydberg electrometry based on electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) with a ground state repumping laser. Though there are many factors that limit the sensitivity of radio frequency field measurements, we show that repumping can enhance the interaction strength while avoiding additional Doppler or power broadening.

title: Wellposedness and scattering for the generalized Boussinesq equation
creator: Jie Chen Boling Guo Jie Shao
description:
A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jie Chen Boling Guo Jie Shao. In this paper, we show the local well-posedness of the generalized Boussinesq equation(gBQ) in
L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{d}),H^{1}(\mathbb{R}^{d})
and obtain the global well-posedness, finite-time blowup and small initial data scattering of gBQ in energy space
H^{1}(\mathbb{R}^{d})
. Moreover, we obtain the large radial initial data scattering of defocusing case for
d\geqslant 3
by using the method of Dodson-Murphy
[
10
]
. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classifications. 35L70; 35Q55; 35A01; 35P25. Key words and phrases.

title: NEUTRINOS AND STRONG INTERACTIONS: QCD (and BEYOND?)
description: Abstract In this talk the answer to the question: what neutrinos have to do with QCD, the present theory of strong interactions? is presented. The answer is positive as some strong arguments on this assertion that are presented bring out.

title: Local systems in diffeology
creator: Katsuhiko KURIBAYASHI
description: Abstract . By making use of Halperin’s local systems over simplicial sets and the model structure of the category of diffeological spaces due to Kihara, we introduce a framework of rational homotopy theory for such smooth spaces with arbitrary fundamental groups.

title: Entanglement Limits in Hybrid Spin-Mechanical Systems
creator: Souvik Agasti, Abhishek Shukla, Milos Nesladek
description: Abstract We investigate how to generate continuous-variable entanglement between distant optomechanical and spin systems, by transferring input two-mode squeezed vacuum state to the system. Such a setup has been proposed for backaction evading gravitational-wave measurement, squeezing the output noise below the standard quantum limit.

title: Adaptive perturbation adversarial training: based on reinforcement learning
creator: Zhishen Nie, Ying Lin, Sp Ren, Lan Zhang
description: Abstract Adversarial training has become the primary method to defend against adversarial samples. However, it is hard to practically apply due to many shortcomings. One of the shortcomings of adversarial training is that it will reduce the recognition accuracy of normal samples. Adaptive perturbation adversarial training is proposed to alleviate this problem.

title: Complete S ​ E ​ ( 3 ) SE(3) invariants for a comeagre set of C 3 C^{3} compact orientable surfaces in ℝ 3 {\mathbb{R}}^{3}
creator: Yair Hayut, David Lehavi
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yair Hayut, David Lehavi. We introduce invariants for compact C 1 C^{1} -orientable surfaces (with boundary) in ℝ 3 {\mathbb{R}}^{3} up to rigid transformations. Our invariants are certain degree four polynomials in the moments of the delta function of the surface. We give an effective and numerically stable inversion algorithm for retrieving the surface from the invariants, which works on a comeagre subset of C 3 C^{3} -surfaces.

title: Fast generation of Cat states in Kerr nonlinear resonators via optimal adiabatic control
creator: Jiao-Jiao Xue 1 , Ke-Hui Yu 1 , Wen-Xiao Liu 2 , Xin Wang 1 and Hong-Rong Li 1
description: Abstract Macroscopic cat states have been widely studied to illustrate fundamental principles of quantum physics as well as their applications in quantum information processing. In this paper, we propose a quantum speedup method for adiabatic creation of cat states in a Kerr nonlinear resonator via optimal adiabatic control.

title: Magnetic reshuffling and feedback on superconductivity in UTe 2 under pressure
creator: M. Vališka, W. Knafo, G. Knebel, G. Lapertot, D. Aoki, D. Braithwaite
description: Abstract The discovery of superconductivity in the heavy-fermion paramagnet UTe 2 has attracted a lot of attention, particularly due to the reinforcement of superconductivity near pressure- and magnetic-field-induced magnetic quantum phase transitions. A challenge is now to characterize the effects of combined pressure and magnetic fields applied along variable directions in this strongly anisotropic paramagnet.

title: Making the Invisible Visible: Risks and Benefits of Disclosing Metadata in Visualization
creator: Alyxander Burns UMass Amherst, Thai On UMass Amherst, Christiana Lee UMass Amherst, Rachel Shapiro Northwestern, Cindy Xiong UMass Amherst, Narges Mahyar UMass Amherst
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Alyxander Burns UMass Amherst, Thai On UMass Amherst, Christiana Lee UMass Amherst, Rachel Shapiro Northwestern, Cindy Xiong UMass Amherst, Narges Mahyar UMass Amherst. Accompanying a data visualization with metadata may benefit readers by facilitating content understanding, strengthening trust, and providing accountability. However, providing this kind of information may also have negative, unintended consequences, such as biasing readers’ interpretations, a loss of trust as a result of too much transparency, and the possibility of opening visualization creators with minoritized identities up to undeserved critique.

title: Equilibrium states of the ice-water front in a differentially heated rectangular cell
creator: Ziqi Wang, Enrico Calzavarini, Chao Sun
description: Abstract We study the conductive and convective states of phase-change of pure water in a rectangular container where two opposite walls are kept respectively at temperatures below and above the freezing point and all the other boundaries are thermally insulating.

title: Background Field Method and Initial-Time Singularity
creator: for Coherent States
description: Abstract The background field method is adopted for studying the dynamics of coherent states within an interacting scalar field theory. Focusing on a coherent state that corresponds to the homogeneous condensate, the quantum depletion of the expectation value of the field-operator is demonstrated to be due to the annihilation of the condensate constituents into relativistic quanta.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning at the Edge of the Statistical Precipice
creator: Rishabh Agarwal, Max Schwarzer, Pablo Samuel Castro, Aaron Courville, Marc G. Bellemare
description: Abstract Deep reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms are predominantly evaluated by comparing their relative performance on a large suite of tasks. Most published results on deep RL benchmarks compare point estimates of aggregate performance such as mean and median scores across tasks, ignoring the statistical uncertainty implied by the use of a finite number of training runs.

title: Companion paper for Well posedness of general cross-diffusion systems
creator: Catherine Choquet
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Catherine Choquet. The paper entitled “Well posedness of general cross-diffusion systems” [ 6 ] is devoted to the mathematical analysis of the Cauchy problem for general cross-diffusion systems without any assumption about its entropic structure. The absence of this type of hypothesis is strongly felt for two questions: the uniqueness of the solution, despite the nonlinear coupling of the highest derivatives terms, and the maximum principle. The article [ 6 ] is therefore largely devoted to these two points.

title: Numerical Eigensolver for Solving Eigenmodes of Cavity Resonators Filled With both Electric and Magnetic Lossy, Anisotropic Media
creator: Wei Jiang 1 , Jie Liu 2 and Shiling Zheng 3
description: Abstract This article presents the numerical eigensolver to find the resonant frequencies of 3-D closed cavity resonators filled with both electric and magnetic lossy, anisotropic media. By introducing a dummy variable with zero value in the 3-D linear vector Maxwell eigenvalue problem for the electric field, we enforce the divergence-free condition for electric flux density in a weak sense.

title: Extracting Qualitative Causal Structure with Transformer-Based NLP
creator: Scott E. Friedman, Ian H. Magnusson, Sonja M. Schmer-Galunder
description: Abstract Qualitative causal relationships compactly express the direction, dependency, temporal constraints, and monotonicity constraints of discrete or continuous interactions in the world. In everyday or academic language, we may express interactions between quantities (e.g., sleep decreases stress), between discrete events or entities (e.g., a protein inhibits another protein’s transcription), or between intentional or functional factors (e.g.

title: VTLayout: Fusion of Visual and Text Features for Document Layout Analysis
creator: Shoubin Li, Xuyan Ma, Shuaiqun Pan, Jun Hu, Lin Shi, Qing Wang
description: Abstract Documents often contain complex physical structures, which make the Document Layout Analysis (DLA) task challenging. As a pre-processing step for content extraction, DLA has the potential to capture rich information in historical or scientific documents on a large scale.

title: Modeling material transport regulation and traffic jam in neurons using PDE-constrained optimization
creator: Angran Li, Yongjie Jessica Zhang*
description: Abstract The intracellular transport process plays an important role in delivering essential materials throughout branched geometries of neurons for their survival and function. Many neurodegenerative diseases have been associated with the disruption of transport. Therefore, it is essential to study how neurons control the transport process to localize materials to necessary locations.

title: Eliminating Systematic Bias from Difference-in-Differences Design: A Permutational Detrending Strategy
creator: Xiaoming Wang, Sukun Wang
description: Abstract Since the initial work by Ashenfelter and Card in 1985, the use of difference-in-differences (DID) study design has become widespread. However, as pointed out in the literature, this popular quasi-experimental design also suffers estimation bias and inference bias, which could be very serious in some circumstances.

title: Perturbation theory for fractional evolution equations in a Banach space
creator: Arzu Ahmadova, Ismail T. Huseynov, Nazim I. Mahmudov
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Arzu Ahmadova, Ismail T. Huseynov, Nazim I. Mahmudov. A strong inspiration for studying perturbation theory for fractional evolution equations comes from the fact that they have proven to be useful tools in modeling many physical processes. In this paper, we study fractional evolution equations of order α ∈ ( 1 , 2 ] \alpha\in(1,2] associated with the infinitesimal generator of an operator fractional cosine function generated by bounded time-dependent perturbations in a Banach space.

title: Optimal multi-wave validation of secondary use data with outcome and exposure misclassification
creator: Sarah C. Lotspeich Department of BiostatisticsVanderbilt University Medical CenterNashville, TN, U.S.A.Department of BiostatisticsUniversity of North Carolina at Chapel HillChapel Hill, NC, U.S.A. lotspes@wfu.edu Gustavo G. C. AmorimDepartment of BiostatisticsVanderbilt University Medical CenterNash
description: Abstract The growing availability of observational databases like electronic health records (EHR) provides unprecedented opportunities for secondary use of such data in biomedical research. However, these data can be error-prone and need to be validated before use. It is usually unrealistic to validate the whole database due to resource constraints.

title: Bayesian Sensitivity Analysis for Missing Data Using the E-value
creator: Wu Xue, Abbas Zaidi
description: Abstract Sensitivity Analysis is a framework to assess how conclusions drawn from missing outcome data may be vulnerable to departures from untestable underlying assumptions. We extend the E-value, a popular metric for quantifying robustness of causal conclusions, to the setting of missing outcomes.

title: Measurement of the γ ​ n → K 0 ​ Σ 0 \gamma n\rightarrow K^{0}\Sigma^{0} differential cross section over the K ∗ K^{*} threshold
creator: K. Kohl, T.C. Jude, S. Alef, R. Beck, A. Braghieri, P.L. Cole, D. Elsner, R. Di Salvo, A. Fantini, O. Freyermuth, F. Frommberger, F. Ghio, A. Gridnev, D. Hammann, J. Hannappel, N. Kozlenko, A. Lapik, P. Levi Sandri, V. Lisin, G. Mandaglio, R. Messi, D. Moricciani, V. Nedorezov, V.A Nikonov, D. Novin
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by K. Kohl, T.C. Jude, S. Alef, R. Beck, A. Braghieri, P.L. Cole, D. Elsner, R. Di Salvo, A. Fantini, O. Freyermuth, F. Frommberger, F. Ghio, A. Gridnev, D. Hammann, J. Hannappel, N. Kozlenko, A. Lapik, P. Levi Sandri, V. Lisin, G. Mandaglio, R. Messi, D. Moricciani, V. Nedorezov, V.A Nikonov, D. Novin.

title: On variants of the Euler sums and symmetric extensions of the Kaneko-Tsumura conjecture
creator: Weiping Wang, Ce Xu [1pt] a . a. School of Science, Zhejiang Sci-Tech University, Hangzhou 310018, P.R. China b . b. School of Mathematics and Statistics, Anhui Normal University, Wuhu 241002, P.R. China
description: Abstract Abstract By using various expansions of the parametric digamma function and the method of residue computations, we study three variants of the linear Euler sums, related Hoffman’s double t -values and Kaneko-Tsumura’s double T -values, and establish several symmetric extensions of the Kaneko-Tsumura conjecture.

title: Vortex lattices in binary Bose-Einstein condensates: Collective modes, quantum fluctuations, and intercomponent entanglement
creator: Takumi Yoshino, Shunsuke Furukawa, Masahito Ueda
description: Abstract We study binary Bose-Einstein condensates subject to synthetic magnetic fields in mutually parallel or antiparallel directions. Within the mean-field theory, the two types of fields have been shown to give the same vortex-lattice phase diagram. We develop an improved effective field theory to study properties of collective modes and ground-state intercomponent entanglement.

title: FedKD: Communication Efficient Federated Learning via Knowledge Distillation
creator: Chuhan Wu Fangzhao Wu Lingjuan Lyu Yongfeng Huang Xing Xie
description: Abstract Federated learning is widely used to learn intelligent models from decentralized data. In federated learning, clients need to communicate their local model updates in each iteration of model learning. However, model updates are large in size if the model contains numerous parameters, and there usually needs many rounds of communication until model converges.

title: A Novel Regularization for Higher Accuracy in the Solution of 3D Stokes Flow
creator: J. Thomas Beale, Christina Jones, Jillian Reale, Svetlana Tlupova
description: Abstract Many problems in fluid dynamics are effectively modeled as Stokes flows - slow, viscous flows where the Reynolds number is small. Boundary integral equations are often used to solve these problems, where the fundamental solutions for the fluid velocity are the Stokeslet and stresslet.

title: Experimental and Numerical Verification of Anomalous Screening Theory in Granular Matter
creator: Chandana Mondal, Michael Moshe, Itamar Procaccia, Saikat Roy, Jin Shang, Jie Zhang
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Chandana Mondal, Michael Moshe, Itamar Procaccia, Saikat Roy, Jin Shang, Jie Zhang. The concept of mechanical screening is widely applied in solid-state systems. Examples include nucleation of defects in crystalline materials, scars and pleats in curved crystals, wrinkles in strongly confined thin sheets, and cell-rearrangements in biological tissue. Available theories of such screening usually contain a crucial ingredient, which is the existence of an ordered reference state, with respect to which screening elements nucleate to release stresses.

title: Representation of binary classification trees with binary features by quantum circuits
creator: Raoul Heese, Patricia Bickert, Astrid Elisa Niederle
description: Abstract We propose a quantum representation of binary classification trees with binary features based on a probabilistic approach. By using the quantum computer as a processor for probability distributions, a probabilistic traversal of the decision tree can be realized via measurements of a quantum circuit.

title: Oxygen Vacancies in Niobium Pentoxide as a Source of Two-Level System Losses in Superconducting Niobium
creator: D. Bafia, A. Murthy, A. Grassellino, A. Romanenko
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by D. Bafia, A. Murthy, A. Grassellino, A. Romanenko. We identify a major source of quantum decoherence in three-dimensional superconducting radio-frequency (SRF) resonators and two-dimensional transmon qubits composed of oxidized niobium: oxygen vacancies in the niobium pentoxide which drive two-level system (TLS) losses.

title: Squared Quartic Hilltop Inflation
creator: Josh Hoffmann, David Sloan
description: Abstract A correction to the Quartic Hilltop inflationary model is proposed to account for stabilising terms in the potential. We derive analytical predictions for the spectral index n s n_{s} and tensor-scalar ratio r r which lie within the Planck 2018 survey bounds.

title: RoboRun: A Robot Runtime to Exploit Spatial Heterogeneity PubID: pubid: 978-1-5386-5541-2/18/$31.00 ©2018 IEEE
creator: Behzad Boroujerdian, Radhika Ghosal, Jonathan Cruz, Brian Plancher, Vijay Janapa Reddi
