title: Scaling effects on the periodic homogenization of a reaction-diffusion-convection problem posed in homogeneous domains connected by a thin composite layer
creator: Vishnu Raveendran, Emilio N.M. Cirillo, Ida de Bonis, Adrian Muntean
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Vishnu Raveendran, Emilio N.M. Cirillo, Ida de Bonis, Adrian Muntean. We study the question of periodic homogenization of a variably scaled reaction-diffusion problem with non-linear drift posed for a domain crossed by a flat composite thin layer. The structure of the non-linearity in the drift was obtained in earlier works as hydrodynamic limit of a totally asymmetric simple exclusion process (TASEP) process for a population of interacting particles crossing a domain with obstacle.

title: Variational Quantum Linear Solver with Dynamic Ansatz
creator: Hrushikesh Patil, Yulun Wang, Predrag S. Krstić
description: Abstract Variational quantum algorithms have found success in the NISQ era owing to their hybrid quantum-classical approach which mitigate the problems of noise in quantum computers. In our study we introduce the dynamic ansatz in the Variational Quantum Linear Solver for a system of linear algebraic equations.

title: Spectral and scattering theory for topological crystals perturbed by infinitely many new edges
creator: S. Richard, N. Tsuzu
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by S. Richard, N. Tsuzu. In this paper we investigate the spectral and scattering theory for operators acting on topological crystals and on their perturbations. A special attention is paid to perturbations obtained by the addition of an infinite number of edges, and / or by the removal of a finite number of them, but perturbations of the underlying measures and perturbations by the addition of a multiplication operator are also considered.

title: Non-Hermitian non-Abelian topological insulators with P ​ T PT symmetry
creator: Motohiko Ezawa
description: Abstract We study a non-Hermitian non-Abelian topological insulator preserving P ​ T PT symmetry, where the non-Hermitian term represents nonreciprocal hoppings. As it increases, a spontaneous P ​ T PT symmetry breaking transition occurs in the perfect-flat band model from a real-line-gap topological insulator into an imaginary-line-gap topological insulator.

title: A conformally invariant Yang-Mills type energy and equation on 6-manifolds Thanks: 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification . primary: 53C18, 53C07; secondary: 58E15, 81T13, 53A55. A.R.G. gratefully acknowledges support from the Royal Society of New Zealand via Marsden Grants 16-UOA-051 and 19-UOA-00
creator: A. Rod Gover, Lawrence J. Peterson, and Callum Sleigh
description: Abstract . We define a conformally invariant action 𝒮 \mathcal{S} on gauge connections on a closed pseudo-Riemannian manifold M M of dimension 6. At leading order this is quadratic in the gauge connection. The Euler-Lagrange equations of 𝒮 \mathcal{S} , with respect to variation of the gauge connection, provide a higher-order conformally invariant analogue of the (source-free) Yang-Mills equations.

title: Parametrized post-Newtonian limit of the Nieh-Yan modified teleparallel gravity
creator: Haomin Rao
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Haomin Rao. The recently proposed Nieh-Yan modified teleparallel gravity is a parity-violating gravity model that modifies the general relativity equivalent teleparallel gravity by a Nieh-Yan term. This model is healthy and simple in form. In this paper, we consider the application of this model to the Solar System and investigate its slow-motion and weak-field approximation in terms of the parametrized post-Newtonian formalism.

title: Mixed spin S=1 and S=½ layered lattice in Cu 2 F 5
creator: Dmitry M. Korotin, Dmitry Y. Novoselov, Vladimir I. Anisimov, Artem R. Oganov
description: Abstract The electronic and magnetic structure, including the Heisenberg model exchange interaction parameters, was explored for the recently proposed novel cuprate Cu 2 F 5 . Using the DFT+U calculation, it is shown that the compound is formed by two types of copper ions with d 9 d^{9} and d 8 d^{8} electronic configurations.

title: Fluctuations in Extractable Work and Bounds on the Charging Power of Quantum Batteries
creator: Shang-Yung Wang
description: Abstract Motivated by a recent disagreement about the claim that fluctuations in the free energy operator bound the charging power of a quantum battery, we present a critical analysis of the original derivation. The analysis shows that the above claim does not hold for both closed- and open-system dynamics.

title: Face.evoLVe : A High-Performance Face Recognition Library
creator: Qingzhong Wang, Pengfei Zhang, Haoyi Xiong, Jian Zhao
description: Abstract . While face recognition has drawn much attention, a large number of algorithms and models have been proposed with applications to daily life, such as authentication for mobile payments, etc. Recently, deep learning methods have dominated in the field of face recognition with advantages in comparisons to conventional approaches and even the human perception.

title: The Future of Solar Neutrinos Journal: Annu. Rev. Nucl. Part. Sci. DOI: 10.1146/annurev-nucl-011921-061243
creator: Gabriel D. Orebi Gann, 1,2 Kai Zuber 3, Daniel Bemmerer, 4 and Aldo Serenelli 5,6,7
description: Abstract In this article we review the current state of the field of solar neutrinos, including flavour oscillations, non-standard effects, solar models, cross section measurements, and the broad experimental program thus motivated and enabled. We discuss the historical discoveries that contributed to current knowledge, and define critical open questions to be addressed in the next decade.

title: The Singular Evolutoids Set and the Extended Evolutoids Front
creator: Michał Zwierzyński
description: Abstract . In this paper we introduce the notion of the singular evolutoid set which is the set of all singular points of all evolutoids of a fixed smooth planar curve with at most cusp singularities. By the Gauss-Bonnet Theorem for Coherent Tangent Bundles over Surfaces with Boundary (Theorem 2.

title: Photocurrent response in parity-time symmetric current-ordered states
creator: Hikaru Watanabe, Youichi Yanase
description: Abstract There is growing interest in the photo-induced generation of rectified current, namely photocurrent phenomenon. While the response was attributed to noncentrosymmetric structures of crystals, the parity violation accompanied by the magnetic ordering, that is, magnetic parity violation, is recently attracting attention as a platform for a photocurrent generator.

title: Data Sharing Markets
creator: Mohammad Rasouli, Michael Jordan
description: Abstract With the growing use of distributed machine learning techniques, there is a growing need for data markets that allows agents to share data with each other. Nevertheless data has unique features that separates it from other commodities including replicability, cost of sharing, and ability to distort.

title: Minimal length, maximal momentum and stochastic gravitational waves spectrum generated from cosmological QCD phase transition
creator: Mohamed Moussa, Homa Shababi, Anisur Rahaman, Ujjal Kumar Dey
description: Abstract We investigate thoroughly the temporal evolution of the universe temperature as a function of the Hubble parameter associated with the Stochastic Gravitational Wave (SGW), that formed at the cosmological QCD phase transition epoch to the current epoch, within the Generalized Uncertainty Principle (GUP) framework.

title: High-order gas-kinetic scheme in general curvilinear coordinate for iLES of compressible wall-bounded turbulent flows
creator: Guiyu Cao, Liang Pan, Minping Wan, Kun Xu, Shiyi Chen
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Guiyu Cao, Liang Pan, Minping Wan, Kun Xu, Shiyi Chen. In this paper, a high-order gas-kinetic scheme in general curvilinear coordinate (HGKS-cur) is developed for the numerical simulation of compressible turbulence. Based on the coordinate transformation, the Bhatnagar-Gross-Krook (BGK) equation is transformed from physical space to computational space. To deal with the general mesh given by discretized points, the geometrical metrics need to be constructed by the dimension-by-dimension Lagrangian interpolation.

title: Input Agnostic Deep Learning for Alzheimer’s Disease Classification Using Multimodal MRI Images
creator: Aidana Massalimova, Huseyin Atakan Varol, Senior Member, IEEE
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Aidana Massalimova, Huseyin Atakan Varol, Senior Member, IEEE. Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a progressive brain disorder that causes memory and functional impairments. The advances in machine learning and publicly available medical datasets initiated multiple studies in AD diagnosis. In this work, we utilize a multi-modal deep learning approach in classifying normal cognition, mild cognitive impairment and AD classes on the basis of structural MRI and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) scans from the OASIS-3 dataset.

title: Origin of the Background Absorption in Carbon Nanotubes: Phonon-Assisted Excitonic Continuum
creator: Stefano Dal Forno, Natsumi Komatsu, Michael Wais, Ali Mojibpour, Indrajit Wadgaonkar, Saunab Ghosh, Yohei Yomogida, Kazuhiro Yanagi, Karsten Held, Junichiro Kono, Marco Battiato
description: Abstract Excitonic effects in 1D semiconductors can be qualitatively different from those in higher dimensions. In particular, the Sommerfeld factor, the ratio of the above-band-edge excitonic continuum absorption to free electron-hole pair generation, has been shown to be less than 1 (i.e., suppressed) in 1D systems while it is larger than 1 (i.e., enhanced) in 2D and 3D systems.

title: Signature of a randomness-driven spin-liquid state in a frustrated magnet
creator: J. Khatua, M. Gomilšek, J. C. Orain, A. M. Strydom, Z. Jagličić, C. V. Colin, S. Petit, A. Ozarowski, L. Mangin-Thro, K. Sethupathi, M.S. Ramachandra Rao, A. Zorko, P. Khuntia
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by J. Khatua, M. Gomilšek, J. C. Orain, A. M. Strydom, Z. Jagličić, C. V. Colin, S. Petit, A. Ozarowski, L. Mangin-Thro, K. Sethupathi, M.S. Ramachandra Rao, A. Zorko, P. Khuntia. Collective behaviour of electrons, frustration induced quantum fluctuations and entanglement in quantum materials underlie some of the emergent quantum phenomena with exotic quasi-particle excitations that are highly relevant for technological applications.

title: Non-degeneracy and quantitative stability of half-harmonic maps from ℝ \mathbb{R} to 𝕊 \mathbb{S}
creator: Bin Deng, Liming Sun, Jun-cheng Wei
description: Abstract . We consider half-harmonic maps from ℝ \mathbb{R} (or 𝕊 \mathbb{S} ) to 𝕊 \mathbb{S} . We prove that all (finite energy) half-harmonic maps are non-degenerate. In other words, they are integrable critical points of the energy functional. A full description of the kernel of the linearized operator around each half-harmonic map is given.

title: Transport away your problems: Calibrating stochastic simulations with optimal transport Journal: Nucl. Instrum. Meth. A
creator: Chris Pollard, Philipp Windischhofer
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Chris Pollard, Philipp Windischhofer. Stochastic simulators are an indispensable tool in many branches of science. Often based on first principles, they deliver a series of samples whose distribution implicitly defines a probability measure to describe the phenomena of interest. However, the fidelity of these simulators is not always sufficient for all scientific purposes, necessitating the construction of ad-hoc corrections to “calibrate” the simulation and ensure that its output is a faithful representation of reality.

title: Ghosts and congruences for p s p^{s} -approximations of hypergeometric periods
creator: Alexander Varchenko ⋆ and Wadim Zudilin ⋄
description: Abstract . We prove general Dwork-type congruences for constant terms attached to tuples of Laurent polynomials. We apply this result to establishing arithmetic and p p -adic analytic properties of functions originating from polynomial solutions modulo p s p^{s} of hypergeometric and KZ equations, solutions which come as coefficients of master polynomials and whose coefficients are integers.

title: Toward the nonequilibrium thermodynamic analog of complexity and the Jarzynski identity
creator: Chen Bai, Wen-hao Li, Xian-hui Ge
description: Abstract The Jarzynski identity can describe small-scale nonequilibrium systems through stochastic thermodynamics. The identity considers fluctuating trajectories in a phase space. The complexity geometry frames the discussions on quantum computational complexity using the method of Riemannian geometry, which builds a bridge between optimal quantum circuits and classical geodesics in the space of unitary operators.

title: ObserveNet Control: A Vision-Dynamics Learning Approach to Predictive Control in Autonomous Vehicles
creator: Cosmin Ginerica 1 , Mihai Zaha 1 , Florin Gogianu 2 , Lucian Busoniu 3 , Bogdan Trasnea 1 , and Sorin Grigorescu 1
description: Abstract A key component in autonomous driving is the ability of the self-driving car to understand, track and predict the dynamics of the surrounding environment. Although there is significant work in the area of object detection, tracking and observations prediction, there is no prior work demonstrating that raw observations prediction can be used for motion planning and control.

title: Perfectness of Kirillov-Reshetikhin Crystals B r , s B^{r,s} for types E 6 ( 1 ) E_{6}^{(1)} and E 7 ( 1 ) E_{7}^{(1)} with a minuscule node r r
creator: Toya Hiroshima
description: Abstract . We prove the perfectness of Kirillov-Reshetikhin crystals B r , s B^{r,s} for types E 6 ( 1 ) E_{6}^{(1)} and E 7 ( 1 ) E_{7}^{(1)} with r r being the minuscule node and s ≥ 1 s\geq 1 using the polytope model of KR crystals introduced by Jang [ 11 ] .

title: Longitudinal charge distribution measurement of non-relativistic ion beams using coherent transition radiation
creator: R. Singh, T. Reichert
description: Abstract 1 Abstract Longitudinal charge profile measurements or bunch shape measurements is a challenge for temporally short non-relativistic bunches. The field profile has a larger longitudinal extent compared to the charge profile for such beams. This affects the ability of field sensing devices such as phase pick-ups or wall current monitors to measure charge distribution.

title: Composition of multipartite quantum systems: perspective from time-like paradigm
creator: Sahil Gopalkrishna Naik, Edwin Peter Lobo, Samrat Sen, Ram Krishna Patra, Mir Alimuddin, Tamal Guha, Some Sankar Bhattacharya, Manik Banik
description: Abstract Figuring out the physical rationale behind natural selection of quantum theory is one of the most acclaimed quests in quantum foundational research. This pursuit has inspired several axiomatic initiatives to derive mathematical formulation of the theory by identifying general structure of state and effect space of individual systems as well as specifying their composition rules.

title: Joint Power and Gain Allocation in MDM-WDM Optical Communication Networks Based on Enhanced Gaussian Noise Model Journal: ao
creator: M. A. Amirabadi, M. H. Kahaei, S. A. Nezamalhosseini
description: Abstract Achieving reliable communication over different channels and modes is one of the main goals of Mode Division Multiplexing-Wavelength Division Multiplexing (MDM-WDM) communication networks. The reliability can be described by minimum Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR) margin which dependents on launched power, Multimode-Erbium Doped Fiber Amplification (MM-EDFA) gain, and MMF nonlinearity.

title: Fabrizio Ferro
description: Abstract Proton reconstruction with the Precision Proton Spectrometer (PPS) in Run 2 and the PPS at HL-LHC 1 INFN, Sezione di Genova (Italy) * fabrizio.ferro@ge.infn.it August 8, 2026 Proceedings for the XXVIII International Workshop on Deep-Inelastic Scattering and Related Subjects, Stony Brook University, New York, USA, 12-16 April 2021 10.21468/SciPostPhysProc.?

title: Transient growth in a flat plate boundary layer under a stream with uniform shear
creator: Shyam Sunder Gopalakrishnan, Alakesh Chandra Mandal
description: Abstract One of the simplest problems involving external vorticity in boundary layer flows is the flow over a semi-infinite plate under a stream of uniform shear. We study the transient growth phenomenon in this flow to investigate the role of freestream shear on energy amplification, and analyse the differences with the Blasius flow.

title: Singularities in L 1 L^{1} -supercritical Fokker–Planck equations: A qualitative analysis
creator: Katharina Hopf
description: Abstract . A class of nonlinear Fokker–Planck equations with superlinear drift is investigated in the L 1 L^{1} -supercritical regime, which exhibits a finite critical mass. The equations have a formal Wasserstein-like gradient-flow structure with a convex mobility and a free energy functional whose minimising measure has a singular component if above the critical mass.

title: On bases of quantum affine algebras Thanks: This review is based on the report of Jie Xiao given in the conference ” Forty Years of Algebraic Groups, Algebraic Geometry, and Representation Theory in China ” in Jan. 5th, 2020 Thanks: ∗ supported by Tsinghua University Initiative Scientific Research P
creator: Jie Xiao, Han Xu ∗, Minghui Zhao
description: Abstract In Memory of Prof. Xihua Cao 1. Introduction Let \textbf{U}^{+} be the positive part of the quantum group U associated with a generalized Cartan matrix A . In the case of finite type, Lusztig constructed the canonical basis B of \textbf{U}^{+} via two approaches ( [ 8 ] ).

title: Compact User-Specific Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces for Uplink Transmission
creator: Kunzan Liu, Zijian Zhang, Linglong Dai, and Lajos Hanzo
description: Abstract Large-scale antenna arrays employed by the base station (BS) constitute an essential next-generation communications technique. However, due to the constraints of size, cost, and power consumption, it is usually considered unrealistic to use a large-scale antenna array at the user side.

title: CETransformer: Casual Effect Estimation via Transformer Based Representation Learning
creator: Zhenyu Guo, Shuai Zheng, Zhizhe Liu, Kun Yan, Zhenfeng Zhu
description: Abstract Treatment effect estimation, which refers to the estimation of causal effects and aims to measure the strength of the causal relationship, is of great importance in many fields but is a challenging problem in practice. As present, data-driven causal effect estimation faces two main challenges, i.e., selection bias and the missing of counterfactual.

title: Triangulating surfaces with bounded energy
creator: Maciej Borodzik, Monika Szczepanowska
description:
A 2021 arXiv research paper by Maciej Borodzik, Monika Szczepanowska. We show that if a closed C 1 C^{1} -smooth surface in a Riemannian manifold has bounded Kolasinski–Menger energy, then it can be triangulated with triangles whose number is bounded by the energy and the area. Each of the triangles is an image of a subset of a plane under a diffeomorphism whose distortion is bounded by 2 \sqrt{2} . 1991 Mathematics Subject Classification
primary: 53A05; secondary: 28A75, 49Q10, 49Q20, 53C21

1.

title: Detection of cross-correlation between CMB Lensing and low-density points
creator: Fuyu Dong, Pengjie Zhang, Le Zhang, Ji Yao, Zeyang Sun, Changbom Park, Xiaohu Yang
description: Abstract Low Density Points (LDPs, Dong et al. 2019 ), obtained by removing high-density regions of observed galaxies, can trace the Large-Scale Structures (LSSs) of the universe. In particular, it offers an intriguing opportunity to detect weak gravitational lensing from low-density regions.

title: Quantum Deep Learning: Sampling Neural Nets with a Quantum Annealer
creator: Catherine F. Higham, Adrian Bedford
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Catherine F. Higham, Adrian Bedford. We demonstrate the feasibility of framing a classically learned deep neural network as an energy based model that can be processed on a one-step quantum annealer in order to exploit fast sampling times. We propose approaches to overcome two hurdles for high resolution image classification on a quantum processing unit (QPU): the required number and binary nature of the model states.

title: The nature of hyperluminous infrared galaxies
creator: F. Gao, L. Wang, A. Efstathiou, K. Małek, P. N. Best, M. Bonato, D. Farrah, R. Kondapally, I. McCheyne, H. J. A. R o ¨ \rm\ddot{o} ttgering
description: Abstract Context. Hyperluminous infrared galaxies (HLIRGs) are shown to have been more abundant in early epochs. The small samples used in earlier studies are not sufficient to draw robust statistical conclusions regarding the physical properties and the power sources of these extreme infrared (IR) bright galaxies. Aims.

title: Deceptive Logic Locking for Hardware Integrity Protection against Machine Learning Attacks
creator: Dominik Sisejkovic, Farhad Merchant, Lennart M. Reimann, and Rainer Leupers
description: Abstract Logic locking has emerged as a prominent key-driven technique to protect the integrity of integrated circuits. However, novel machine-learning-based attacks have recently been introduced to challenge the security foundations of locking schemes. These attacks are able to recover a significant percentage of the key without having access to an activated circuit.

title: Uncertainty-aware Cardinality Estimation by Neural Network Gaussian Process
creator: Kangfei Zhao, Jeffrey Xu Yu, Zongyan He, Hao Zhang
description: Abstract . Deep Learning (DL) has achieved great success in many real applications. Despite its success, there are some main problems when deploying advanced DL models in database systems, such as hyper-parameters tuning, the risk of overfitting, and lack of prediction uncertainty.

title: On the geometric phase and Majorana neutrinos
creator: A. Capolupo, S.M. Giampaolo, B. C. Hiesmayr, G. Lambiase, A. Quaranta
description: Abstract We analyze the geometric phase for neutrinos and we demonstrate that the geometric invariants associated to transitions between different neutrino flavors, for Majorana neutrinos, can depend on the representation of the mixing matrix and then are sensitive to the nature of neutrinos.

title: RGB photometric calibration of 15 million Gaia stars 2021 RGB photometric calibration of 15 million Gaia stars – A.2
creator: Nicolás Cardiel, Jaime Zamorano, Josep Manel Carrasco, Eduard Masana, Salvador Bará, Rafael González, Jaime Izquierdo, Sergio Pascual, Alejandro Sánchez de Miguel
description: Abstract Although a catalogue of synthetic RGB magnitudes, providing photometric data for a sample of 1346 bright stars, has been recently published, its usefulness is still limited due to the small number of reference stars available, considering that they are distributed throughout the whole celestial sphere, and the fact that they are restricted to Johnson V < 6.6 V<6.6 mag.

title: Hidden charm pentaquark states in a diquark model
creator: Pan-Pan Shi, Fei Huang, Wen-Ling Wang
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Pan-Pan Shi, Fei Huang, Wen-Ling Wang. The mass spectrum of hidden charm pentaquark states composed of two diquarks and an antiquark are calculated by use of an effective Hamiltonian which includes explicitly the spin, color, and flavor dependent interactions.

title: Global strong solutions and optimal L 2 L^{2} decay to the compressible FENE dumbbell model
creator: Zhaonan Luo, Wei Luo and, Zhaoyang Yin
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Zhaonan Luo, Wei Luo and, Zhaoyang Yin. In this paper, we are concerned with the global well-posedness and L 2 L^{2} decay rate for the strong solutions of the compressible finite extensible nonlinear elastic (FENE) dumbbell model. For d ≥ 2 d\geq 2 , we prove that the compressible FENE dumbbell model admits a unique global strong solution provided the initial data are close to equilibrium state.

title: Speckle decorrelation in fundamental and second-harmonic light scattered from nonlinear disorder
creator: Rabisankar Samanta, Romain Pierrat, Rémi Carminati, Sushil Mujumdar
description: Abstract Speckle patterns generated in a disordered medium carry a lot of information despite the apparent complete randomness in the intensity pattern. When the medium possesses χ ( 2 ) \chi^{(2)} nonlinearity, the speckle is sensitive to the phase of the incident fundamental light, as well as the light generated within.

title: E-PDDL: A Standardized Way of Defining Epistemic Planning Problems
creator: Francesco Fabiano, Biplav Srivastava, Marianna Bergamaschi Ganapini, Jonathan Lenchner, Lior Horesh, Francesca Rossi
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Francesco Fabiano, Biplav Srivastava, Marianna Bergamaschi Ganapini, Jonathan Lenchner, Lior Horesh, Francesca Rossi. Epistemic Planning (EP) refers to an automated planning setting where the agent reasons in the space of knowledge states and tries to find a plan to reach a desirable state from the current state. Its general form, the Multi-agent Epistemic Planning (MEP) problem involves multiple agents who need to reason about both the state of the world and the information flow between agents.

title: Quantum characteristic classes, moment correspondences and the Hamiltonian groups of coadjoint orbits
creator: Chi Hong Chow
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Chi Hong Chow. For any coadjoint orbit G / L G/L , we determine all useful terms of the associated Savelyev-Seidel morphism defined on H − ⁣ ∗ ​ ( Ω ​ G ) H_{-*}(\Omega G) .

title: Adversarial Continual Learning for Multi-Domain Hippocampal Segmentation Supported by the Bundesministerium für Gesundheit (BMG) with grant [ZMVI1- 2520DAT03A]. The final version of this manuscript will be published in Springer Lecture Notes in Computer Science, Domain Adaptation and Representation
creator: Marius Memmel, Camila Gonzalez, Anirban Mukhopadhyay
description: Abstract Deep learning for medical imaging suffers from temporal and privacy-related restrictions on data availability. To still obtain viable models, continual learning aims to train in sequential order, as and when data is available. The main challenge that continual learning methods face is to prevent catastrophic forgetting, i.e., a decrease in performance on the data encountered earlier.

title: Influence of a Set of Variables on a Boolean Function
creator: Aniruddha Biswas, Palash Sarkar
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Aniruddha Biswas, Palash Sarkar. The influence of a variable is an important concept in the analysis of Boolean functions. The more general notion of influence of a set of variables on a Boolean function has four separate definitions in the literature. In the present work, we introduce a new definition of influence of a set of variables which is based on the auto-correlation function and develop its basic theory.

title: Delay-Compensated Distributed PDE Control of Traffic with Connected/Automated Vehicles
creator: Jie Qi, Shurong Mo, Miroslav Krstic
description: Abstract We develop an input delay-compensating design for stabilization of an Aw-Rascle-Zhang (ARZ) traffic model in congested regime which is governed by a 2 × 2 2\times 2 first-order hyperbolic nonlinear PDE. The traffic flow consists of both adaptive cruise control-equipped (ACC-equipped) and manually-driven vehicles.

title: Attribution of Predictive Uncertainties in Classification Models
creator: Iker Perez, Piotr Skalski, Alec Barns-Graham, Jason Wong, David Sutton
description: Abstract Predictive uncertainties in classification tasks are often a consequence of model inadequacy or insufficient training data. In popular applications, such as image processing, we are often required to scrutinise these uncertainties by meaningfully attributing them to input features. This helps to improve interpretability assessments. However, there exist few effective frameworks for this purpose.

title: Black-Hole Neutron Star Simulations with the BAM code: First Tests and Simulations
creator: Swami Vivekanandji Chaurasia 1, Tim Dietrich 2,3, Stephan Rosswog 1
description: Abstract The first detections of black hole - neutron star mergers (GW200105 and GW200115) by the LIGO-Virgo-Kagra Collaboration mark a significant scientific breakthrough. The physical interpretation of pre- and post-merger signals requires careful cross-examination between observational and theoretical modelling results.

title: Two-neutrino double-beta decay matrix elements based on relativistic nuclear energy density functional
creator: N. Popara, A. Ravlić, N. Paar
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by N. Popara, A. Ravlić, N. Paar. Nuclear matrix elements (NMEs) for two-neutrino double-beta decay ( 2 ​ ν ​ β ​ β 2\nu\beta\beta ) are studied in the framework of relativistic nuclear energy density functional (REDF). The properties of nuclei involved in the decay are obtained using the relativistic Hartree-Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer theory and relevant nuclear transitions are described using the relativistic proton-neutron quasiparticle random phase approximation based on relativistic energy density functional (REDF-QRPA).

title: Estimation of high-dimensional change-points under a group sparsity structure
creator: Hanqing Cai, Tengyao Wang
description: Abstract Change-points are a routine feature of ‘big data’ observed in the form of high-dimensional data streams. In many such data streams, the component series possess group structures and it is natural to assume that changes only occur in a small number of all groups.

title: Adaptive Transfer Learning on Graph Neural Networks Conference: Proceedings of the 27th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining; August 14–18, 2021; Virtual Event, Singapore Proceedings of the 27th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (KDD ’21), August 14
creator: Xueting Han, Zhenhuan Huang, Bang An, Jing Bai
description: Abstract . Graph neural networks (GNNs) is widely used to learn a powerful representation of graph-structured data. Recent work demonstrates that transferring knowledge from self-supervised tasks to downstream tasks could further improve graph representation. However, there is an inherent gap between self-supervised tasks and downstream tasks in terms of optimization objective and training data.

title: Can Multi-Threaded Flux Tubes in Coronal Arcades Support a Magnetohydrodynamic Avalanche?
creator: J. Threlfall, J. Reid, A.W. Hood
description: Abstract keywords Magnetic fields, corona; Magnetohydrodynamics; Magnetic flux tubes; Magnetohydrodynamic avalanche; Magnetic reconnection, theory \setlastpage \inarticletrue {opening} 1 Introduction \ilabel sec:intro Despite incredible advances, in both observations and modelling, our understanding of the exact means through which magnetic energy is released in the solar corona remains limited.

title: VisDrone-CC2020: The Vision Meets Drone Crowd Counting Challenge Results
creator: Dawei Du 1, Longyin Wen 2, Pengfei Zhu 3, Heng Fan 4, Qinghua Hu 3, Haibin Ling 4, Mubarak Shah 5, Junwen Pan 3, Ali Al-Ali 21, Amr Mohamed 12, Bakour Imene 14, Bin Dong 11, Binyu Zhang 13, Bouchali Hadia Nesma 14, Chenfeng Xu 6, Chenzhen Duan 20, Ciro Castiello 16, Corrado Mencar 16, Dingkang Liang
description: Abstract Crowd counting on the drone platform is an interesting topic in computer vision, which brings new challenges such as small object inference, background clutter and wide viewpoint. However, there are few algorithms focusing on crowd counting on the drone-captured data due to the lack of comprehensive datasets.

title: Precise Aerial Image Matching based on Deep Homography Estimation
creator: Myeong-Seok Oh, Yong-Ju Lee, Seong-Whan Lee
description: Abstract Aerial image registration or matching is a geometric process of aligning two aerial images captured in different environments. Estimating the precise transformation parameters is hindered by various environments such as time, weather, and viewpoints. The characteristics of the aerial images are mainly composed of a straight line owing to building and road.

title: Supplying angular momentum to the jittering jets explosion mechanism using inner convection layers
creator: Dmitry Shishkin, Noam Soker
description: Abstract We conduct one-dimensional stellar evolution simulations in the mass range 13 − 20 ​ M ⊙ 13-20M_{\odot} to late core collapse times and find that an inner vigorous convective zone with large specific angular momentum fluctuations appears at the edge of the iron core during the collapse.

title: Joint Dermatological Lesion Classification and Confidence Modeling with Uncertainty Estimation
creator: Gun-Hee Lee, Han-Bin Ko, Seong-Whan Lee
description: Abstract Deep learning has played a major role in the interpretation of dermoscopic images for detecting skin defects and abnormalities. However, current deep learning solutions for dermatological lesion analysis are typically limited in providing probabilistic predictions which highlights the importance of concerning uncertainties.

title: Optimizing Gait Libraries via a Coverage Metric
creator: Brian Bittner, Shai Revzen
description: Abstract Many robots move through the world by composing locomotion primitives like steps and turns. To do so well, robots need not have primitives that make intuitive sense to humans. This becomes of paramount importance when robots are damaged and no longer move as designed.

title: Federated Learning with Dynamic Transformer for Text to Speech
creator: Zhenhou Hong, Jianzong Wang*, Xiaoyang Qu, Jie Liu, Chendong Zhao, Jing Xiao
description: Abstract Text to speech (TTS) is a crucial task for user interaction, but TTS model training relies on a sizable set of high-quality original datasets. Due to privacy and security issues, the original datasets are usually unavailable directly. Recently, federated learning proposes a popular distributed machine learning paradigm with an enhanced privacy protection mechanism.

title: How does a robot’s social credibility relate to its perceived trustworthiness?
creator: Patrick Holthaus
description: Abstract I Introduction This position paper aims to highlight and discuss the role of a robot’s social credibility in interaction with humans. In particular, I want to explore a potential relation between social credibility and a robot’s acceptability and ultimately its trustworthiness.

title: Cobordisms and commutative categorial grammars
creator: Sergey Slavnov
description: Abstract We propose a concrete surface representation of abstract categorial grammars in the category of word cobordisms or cowordisms for short, which are certain bipartite graphs decorated with words in a given alphabet, generalizing linear logic proof-nets. We also introduce and study linear logic grammars , directly based on cobordisms and using classical multiplicative linear logic as a typing system.

title: The physical properties of γ \gamma -ray quiet flat-spectrum radio quasars: why are they undetected by F ​ e ​ r ​ m ​ i Fermi -LAT? 2021 The physical properties of γ \gamma -ray quiet flat-spectrum radio quasars: why are they undetected by F ​ e ​ r ​ m ​ i Fermi -LAT? – 2
creator: Xue-Jiao Deng, Rui Xue, Ze-Rui Wang, Shao-Qiang Xi, Hu-Bing Xiao, Lei-Ming Du and Zhao-Hua Xie
description: Abstract During a decade of the F ​ e ​ r ​ m ​ i Fermi -Large Area Telescope (LAT) operation, thousands of blazars have been detected in the γ \gamma -ray band. However, there are still numbers of blazars that have not been detected in the γ \gamma -ray band.

title: Semiclassical propagation of coherent states and wave packets: hidden saddles
creator: Huichao Wang and Steven Tomsovic
description: Abstract Semiclassical methods are extremely important in the subjects of wave packet and coherent state dynamics. Unfortunately, these essentially saddle point approximations are considered nearly impossible to carry out in detail for systems with multiple degrees of freedom due to the difficulties of solving the resulting two-point boundary value problems.

title: On Out-of-distribution Detection with Energy-based Models
creator: Sven Elflein, Bertrand Charpentier, Daniel Zügner, Stephan Günnemann, Sven Elflein, Bertrand Charpentier, Daniel Zügner, Stephan Günnemann
description: Abstract Several density estimation methods have shown to fail to detect out-of-distribution (OOD) samples by assigning higher likelihoods to anomalous data. Energy-based models (EBMs) are flexible, unnormalized density models which seem to be able to improve upon this failure mode.

title: One-Class Classification for Wafer Map using Adversarial Autoencoder with DSVDD Prior
creator: Ha Young Jo, Seong-Whan Lee
description: Abstract Recently, semiconductors’ demand has exploded in virtual reality, smartphones, wearable devices, the internet of things, robotics, and automobiles. Semiconductor manufacturers want to make semiconductors with high yields. To do this, manufacturers conduct many quality assurance activities. Wafer map pattern classification is a typical way of quality assurance.

title: UVES analysis of red giants in the bulge globular cluster NGC 6522 Thanks: Observations collected at the European Southern Observatory, Paranal, Chile (ESO), under programmes 088.D-0398A, and 097.D-0175 (PI: B. Barbuy), 071.B-0617, 73.B-0074 (PI: A. Renzini.). Preprint: B. Barbuy
creator: B. Barbuy, E. Cantelli, L. Muniz, S.O. Souza, C. Chiappini, R. Hirschi, G. Cescutti, M. Pignatari, S. Ortolani, L. Kerber, F.F.S. Maia, E. Bica, E. Depagne
description: Abstract Context. NGC 6522 is a moderately metal-poor bulge globular cluster ([Fe/H] ∼ \sim − - 1.0), and it is a well-studied representative among a number of moderately metal-poor blue horizontal branch clusters located in the bulge. The NGC 6522 abundance pattern can give hints on the earliest chemical enrichment in the central Galaxy. Aims.

title: Assessing competitive balance in the English Premier League for over forty seasons using a stochastic block model
creator: Francesca BasiniVasiliki Tsouli, Ioannis Ntzoufras, Nial Friel
description: Abstract Competitive balance is the subject of much interest in the sports analytics literature and beyond. In this paper, we develop a statistical network model based on an extension of the stochastic block model to assess the balance between teams in a league.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Quantum State Preparation with Weak Nonlinear Measurements
creator: Riccardo Porotti, Antoine Essig, Benjamin Huard, Florian Marquardt
description: Abstract Quantum control has been of increasing interest in recent years, e.g. for tasks like state initialization and stabilization. Feedback-based strategies are particularly powerful, but also hard to find, due to the exponentially increased search space. Deep reinforcement learning holds great promise in this regard.

title: Boost-R: Gradient Boosted Trees for Recurrence Data
creator: Xiao Liu, Rong Pan
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Xiao Liu, Rong Pan. Recurrence data arise from multi-disciplinary domains spanning reliability, cyber security, healthcare, online retailing, etc. This paper investigates an additive-tree-based approach, known as Boost-R (Boosting for Recurrence Data), for recurrent event data with both static and dynamic features.

title: Revealing higher-order light and matter energy exchanges using quantum trajectories in ultrastrong coupling
creator: Vincenzo Macrì, Fabrizio Minganti, Anton Frisk Kockum, Alessandro Ridolfo, Salvatore Savasta, Franco Nori
description: Abstract The dynamics of open quantum systems is often modelled using master equations, which describe the expected outcome of an experiment (i.e., the average over many realizations of the same dynamics). Quantum trajectories, instead, model the outcome of ideal single experiments—the “clicks” of a perfect detector due to, e.g., spontaneous emission.

title: Exploring the efficacy of neural networks for trajectory compression and the inverse problem
creator: Theodoros Ntakouris
description: Abstract In this document, a neural network is employed in order to estimate the solution of the initial value problem in the context of non linear trajectories. Such trajectories can be subject to gravity, thrust, drag, centrifugal force, temperature, ambient air density and pressure.

title: Visual Adversarial Imitation Learning using Variational Models
creator: Rafael Rafailov Tianhe Yu Aravind Rajeswaran Chelsea Finn[2pt] {rafailov, tianheyu, cbfinn}@stanford.edu, aravraj@fb.com, [2pt] Stanford University, University of Washington, Facebook AI Research
description: Abstract Reward function specification, which requires considerable human effort and iteration, remains a major impediment for learning behaviors through deep reinforcement learning. In contrast, providing visual demonstrations of desired behaviors often presents an easier and more natural way to teach agents.

title: Ab Initio Particle-based Object Manipulation
creator: Siwei Chen, Xiao Ma, Yunfan Lu and David Hsu
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Siwei Chen, Xiao Ma, Yunfan Lu and David Hsu. Particle-based Object Manipulation ( PROMPT ) is a new method for robot manipulation of novel objects, without prior object models or pre-training on a large object data set. The key element of PROMPT is a particle-based object representation, in which each particle represents a point in an object, the local geometric, physical, and other features of the point, and also its relation with other particles. The particle representation connects visual perception with robot control.

title: Relative Localization of Mobile Robots with Multiple Ultra-WideBand Ranging Measurements Thanks: This work is supported by National Key R&D Program of China (2019YFB1310805). Z. Cao, R. Liu, C. Yuen, A. Athukorala, B. K. K. Ng, U-X. Tan are with the Singapore University of Technology and Design, 8 S
creator: Zhiqiang Cao, Ran Liu, Chau Yuen, Achala Athukorala, Benny Kai Kiat Ng
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Zhiqiang Cao, Ran Liu, Chau Yuen, Achala Athukorala, Benny Kai Kiat Ng. Relative localization between autonomous robots without infrastructure is crucial to achieve their navigation, path planning, and formation in many applications, such as emergency response, where acquiring a prior knowledge of the environment is not possible. The traditional Ultra-WideBand (UWB)-based approach provides a good estimation of the distance between the robots, but obtaining the relative pose (including the displacement and orientation) remains challenging.

title: An inverse problem of determining the orders of systems of fractional pseudo-differential equations
creator: Ravshan Ashurov, Sabir Umarov
description: Abstract . As it is known various dynamical processes can be modeled through the systems of time-fractional order pseudo-differential equations. In the modeling process one frequently faces with determining adequate orders of time-fractional derivatives in the sense of Riemann-Liouville or Caputo. This problem is qualified as an inverse problem. The right (vector) order can be found utilizing the available data.

title: Renyi Differential Privacy of the Subsampled Shuffle Model in Distributed Learning
creator: Antonious M. Girgis, Deepesh Data, Suhas Diggavi
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Antonious M. Girgis, Deepesh Data, Suhas Diggavi. We study privacy in a distributed learning framework, where clients collaboratively build a learning model iteratively through interactions with a server from whom we need privacy. Motivated by stochastic optimization and the federated learning (FL) paradigm, we focus on the case where a small fraction of data samples are randomly sub-sampled in each round to participate in the learning process, which also enables privacy amplification.

title: A Holographic Superfluid Symphony
creator: Daniel Areán, Matteo Baggioli, Sebastian Grieninger, and Karl Landsteiner
description: Abstract We study the hydrodynamic excitations of backreacted holographic superfluids by computing the full set of quasinormal modes (QNMs) at finite momentum and matching them to the existing hydrodynamic theory of superfluids. Additionally, we analyze the behavior of the low-energy excitations in real frequency and complex momentum, going beyond the standard QNM picture.

title: RingFed: Reducing Communication Costs in Federated Learning on Non-IID Data
creator: Guang Yang, Ke Mu, Chunhe Song, Zhijia Yang, and Tierui Gong
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Guang Yang, Ke Mu, Chunhe Song, Zhijia Yang, and Tierui Gong. Federated learning is a widely used distributed deep learning framework that protects the privacy of each client by exchanging model parameters rather than raw data. However, federated learning suffers from high communication costs, as a considerable number of model parameters need to be transmitted many times during the training process, making the approach inefficient, especially when the communication network bandwidth is limited.

title: Sensitivity of string compressors and repetitiveness measures
creator: Tooru Akagi, Mitsuru Funakoshi, Shunsuke Inenaga
description: Abstract The sensitivity of a string compression algorithm C C asks how much the output size C ⁡ ( T ) C(T) for an input string T T can increase when a single character edit operation is performed on T T .

title: Auctions with Interdependence and SOS: Improved Approximation
creator: Ameer Amer, Inbal Talgam-Cohen
description: Abstract Interdependent values make basic auction design tasks – in particular maximizing welfare truthfully in single-item auctions – quite challenging. Eden et al. recently established that if bidders’ valuation functions are submodular over their signals (a.k.a. SOS), a truthful 4-approximation to the optimal welfare exists.

title: Machine learning application to detect light echoes around black holes 2021 Machine learning application to detect light echoes around black holes – References
creator: P. Chainakun, N. Mankatwit, P. Thongkonsing, A. J. Young
description: Abstract X-ray reverberation has become a powerful tool to probe the disc-corona geometry near black holes. Here, we develop Machine Learning (ML) models to extract the X-ray reverberation features imprinted in the Power Spectral Density (PSD) of AGN. The machine is trained using simulated PSDs in the form of a simple power-law encoded with the relativistic echo features.

title: A new method of carbon budget analysis with application to present and paleo atmospheric concentration data sets
creator: Alice Nadeau, Richard McGehee, Clarence Lehman
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Alice Nadeau, Richard McGehee, Clarence Lehman. We introduce a new method for analyzing the carbon budget using box models and a mass balance approach. The method describes the net flow of carbon between the atmosphere and other reservoirs. The method assumes that the data can be explained by having the carbon move in and out of the atmosphere through two reservoirs, one consisting of isotopically light carbon (biotic) and the other consisting of isotopically heavy carbon (abiotic).

title: Constructing uncountably many groups with the same profinite completion
creator: Nikolay Nikolov, Dan Segal
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Nikolay Nikolov, Dan Segal. To what extent is a finitely generated residually finite (f.g.r.f.) group determined by its finite quotients? This question can be formulated in various ways, see for example [ GZ ] . The family of all finite quotients of a group G is determined by its inverse limit, the profinite completion \widehat{G} ; following [ GZ ] let us define the genus of an f.g.r.f. group G to be the set of isomorphism classes of f.g.r.f.

title: Multimodal Reward Shaping for Efficient Exploration in Reinforcement Learning
creator: Mingqi Yuan, Man-on Pun, Dong Wang, Yi Chen, Haojun Li, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen, Shenzhen Research Institute of Big Data {mingqiyuan, haojunli}@link.cuhk.edu.cn{simonpun,yichen,wangdong}@cuhk.edu.cn
description: Abstract Maintaining the long-term exploration capability of the agent remains one of the critical challenges in deep reinforcement learning. A representative solution is to leverage reward shaping to provide intrinsic rewards for the agent to encourage exploration. However, most existing methods suffer from vanishing intrinsic rewards, which cannot provide sustainable exploration incentives.

title: Unsupervised Embedding Learning from Uncertainty Momentum Modeling
creator: Jiahuan Zhou, Yansong Tang, Bing Su, Ying Wu
description: Abstract Existing popular unsupervised embedding learning methods focus on enhancing the instance-level local discrimination of the given unlabeled images by exploring various negative data. However, the existed sample outliers which exhibit large intra-class divergences or small inter-class variations severely limit their learning performance. We justify that the performance limitation is caused by the gradient vanishing on these sample outliers.

title: A Measure Theoretical Approach to the Mean-field Maximum Principle for Training NeurODEs
creator: Benoît Bonnet, Cristina Cipriani, Massimo Fornasier, Hui Huang
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Benoît Bonnet, Cristina Cipriani, Massimo Fornasier, Hui Huang. In this paper we consider a measure-theoretical formulation of the training of NeurODEs in the form of a mean-field optimal control with L 2 L^{2} -regularization of the control. We derive first order optimality conditions for the NeurODE training problem in the form of a mean-field maximum principle, and show that it admits a unique control solution, which is Lipschitz continuous in time.

title: MEGEX: Data-Free Model Extraction Attack against Gradient-Based Explainable AI
creator: Takayuki Miura, Satoshi Hasegawa, Toshiki Shibahara
description: Abstract The advance of explainable artificial intelligence, which provides reasons for its predictions, is expected to accelerate the use of deep neural networks in the real world like Machine Learning as a Service (MLaaS) that returns predictions on queried data with the trained model. Deep neural networks deployed in MLaaS face the threat of model extraction attacks.

title: Universal criticality of thermodynamic geometry for boundary conformal field theories in gauge/gravity duality
creator: Morteza Rafiee a, Seyed Ali Hosseini Mansoori a, Shao-Wen Wei b,c, Robert B. Mann d,e
description: Abstract According to more recent AdS/CFT interpretation Karch:2015rpa , in which varying cosmological constant Λ \Lambda in the bulk corresponds to varying the curvature radius governing the space on which the field theory resides, we study the criticality of thermodynamic curvatures for thermal boundary conformal field theories (CFT) that are dual to d d -dimensional charged anti-de Sitter (AdS) black

title: Data Partition and Rate Control for Learning and Energy Efficient Edge Intelligence
creator: Xiaoyang Li, Member, IEEE, Shuai Wang, Member, IEEE, Guangxu Zhu, Member, IEEE, Ziqin Zhou, Student Member, IEEE, Kaibin Huang, Fellow, IEEE, Yi Gong, Senior Member, IEEE
description: Abstract The rapid development of artificial intelligence together with the powerful computation capabilities of the advanced edge servers make it possible to deploy learning tasks at the wireless network edge, which is dubbed as edge intelligence (EI). The communication bottleneck between the data resource and the server results in deteriorated learning performance as well as tremendous energy consumption.

title: Cellular chain complexes of universal covers of some 3-manifolds
description: Abstract For a closed 3-manifold M M in a certain class, we give a presentation of the cellular chain complex of the universal cover of M M . The class includes all surface bundles, some surgeries of knots in S 3 S^{3} , some cyclic branched cover of S 3 S^{3} , and some Seifert manifolds.

title: Damped Dirac magnon in a metallic kagomé antiferromagnet FeSn
creator: Seung-Hwan Do, Koji Kaneko, Ryoichi Kajimoto, Kazuya Kamazawa, Matthew B. Stone, Shinichi Itoh, Takatsugu Masuda, German D. Samolyuk, Elbio Dagotto, William R. Meier, Brian C. Sales, Hu Miao, Andrew D. Christianson
description: Abstract The kagomé lattice is a fertile platform to explore topological excitations with both Fermi-Dirac and Bose-Einstein statistics. While relativistic Dirac Fermions and flat-bands have been discovered in the electronic structure of kagomé metals, the spin excitations have received less attention. Here we report inelastic neutron scattering studies of the prototypical kagomé magnetic metal FeSn.

title: Conformal Symplectic structures, Foliations and Contact Structures
creator: Mélanie Bertelson, Gaël Meigniez
description: Abstract . This paper presents two existence h-principles, the first for conformal symplectic structures on closed manifolds, and the second for leafwise conformal symplectic structures on foliated manifolds with non empty boundary. The latter h-principle allows to linearly deform certain codimension- 1 1 foliations to contact structures.

title: Diagnosing the cosmic coincidence problem and its evolution with recent observations
creator: Jie Zheng 1 ,Yun Chen 2,3,∗ ,Tengpeng Xu 2,3 and Zong-Hong Zhu 1,4
description: Abstract In the framework of a phenomenological cosmological model with the assumption of ρ X ∝ ρ m ​ a ξ \rho_{X}\propto\rho_{m}a^{\xi} ( ρ X \rho_{X} and ρ m \rho_{m} are the energy densities of dark energy and matter, respectively.

title: The final twist: A model of gravitational waves from precessing black-hole binaries through merger and ringdown
creator: Eleanor Hamilton, Lionel London, Jonathan E. Thompson, Edward Fauchon-Jones, Mark Hannam, Chinmay Kalaghatgi, Sebastian Khan, Francesco Pannarale, Alex Vano-Vinuales
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Eleanor Hamilton, Lionel London, Jonathan E. Thompson, Edward Fauchon-Jones, Mark Hannam, Chinmay Kalaghatgi, Sebastian Khan, Francesco Pannarale, Alex Vano-Vinuales. We present PhenomPNR , a frequency-domain phenomenological model of the gravitational-wave (GW) signal from binary-black-hole mergers that is tuned to numerical relativity (NR) simulations of precessing binaries.

title: Generalized Outer Bounds on the Finite Geometric Sum of Ellipsoids
creator: Navid Hashemi, Justin Ruths
description: Abstract General results on convex bodies are reviewed and used to derive an exact closed-form parametric formula for the boundary of the geometric (Minkowski) sum of k k ellipsoids in n n -dimensional Euclidean space. Previously this was done through iterative algorithms in which each new ellipsoid was added to an ellipsoid approximation of the sum of the previous ellipsoids.

title: Optimal Design of Responsive Structures
creator: Andrew Akerson, Blaise Bourdin, Kaushik Bhattacharya
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Andrew Akerson, Blaise Bourdin, Kaushik Bhattacharya. With recent advances in both responsive materials and fabrication techniques it is now possible to construct integrated functional structures, composed of both structural and active materials. We investigate the robust design of such structures through topology optimization. By applying a typical interpolation scheme and filtering technique, we prove existence of an optimal design to a class of objective functions which depend on the compliances of the stimulated and unstimulated states.

title: Introducing a Family of Synthetic Datasets for Research on Bias in Machine Learning
creator: William Blanzeisky, Pádraig Cunningham, Kenneth Kennedy
description: Abstract A significant impediment to progress in research on bias in machine learning (ML) is the availability of relevant datasets. This situation is unlikely to change much given the sensitivity of such data. For this reason there is a role for synthetic data in this research. In this short paper we present one such family of synthetic data sets.

title: Measurement of the Thulium Ion Spin Hamiltonian Within a Yttrium Gallium Garnet Host Crystal
creator: Jacob H. Davidson, Philip J.T. Woodburn, Aaron D. Marsh, Kyle J. Olson, Adam Olivera, Antariksha Das, Mohsen Falamarzi Askarani, Wolfgang Tittel, Rufus L. Cone, Charles W. Thiel
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jacob H. Davidson, Philip J.T. Woodburn, Aaron D. Marsh, Kyle J. Olson, Adam Olivera, Antariksha Das, Mohsen Falamarzi Askarani, Wolfgang Tittel, Rufus L. Cone, Charles W. Thiel. We characterize the magnetic properties for thulium ion energy levels in the Y 3 Ga 5 O 12 (Tm:YGG) lattice with the goal to improve decoherence and reduce line-width broadening caused by local host spins and crystal imperfections.

title: Effects of a pestilent species on the stability of cyclically dominant species Journal: Chaos Solitons and Fractals
creator: D. Bazeia, M. Bongestab, B.F. de Oliveira, A. Szolnoki
description: Abstract Cyclic dominance is frequently believed to be a mechanism that maintains diversity of competing species. But this delicate balance could also be fragile if some of the members is weakened because an extinction of a species will involve the annihilation of its predator hence leaving only a single species alive.

title: On the distribution of the Hodge locus
creator: Gregorio Baldi, Bruno Klingler, and Emmanuel Ullmo
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Gregorio Baldi, Bruno Klingler, and Emmanuel Ullmo. Given a polarizable ℤ \mathbb{Z} -variation of Hodge structures 𝕍 \mathbb{V} over a complex smooth quasi-projective base S S , a classical result of Cattani, Deligne and Kaplan says that its Hodge locus (i.e. the locus where exceptional Hodge tensors appear) is a countable union of irreducible algebraic subvarieties of S S , called the special subvarieties for 𝕍 \mathbb{V} .

title: Electron-loss-to-continuum cusp in collisions of U 89+ with N 2 and Xe
creator: P.-M. Hillenbrand, K. N. Lyashchenko, S. Hagmann, O. Yu. Andreev, D. Banaś, E. P. Benis, A. I. Bondarev, C. Brandau, E. De Filippo, O. Forstner, J. Glorius, R. E. Grisenti, A. Gumberidze, D. L. Guo, M. O. Herdrich, M. Lestinsky, Yu. A. Litvinov, E. V. Pagano, N. Petridis, M. S. Sanjari, D. Schury, U
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by P.-M. Hillenbrand, K. N. Lyashchenko, S. Hagmann, O. Yu. Andreev, D. Banaś, E. P. Benis, A. I. Bondarev, C. Brandau, E. De Filippo, O. Forstner, J. Glorius, R. E. Grisenti, A. Gumberidze, D. L. Guo, M. O. Herdrich, M. Lestinsky, Yu. A. Litvinov, E. V. Pagano, N. Petridis, M. S. Sanjari, D. Schury, U.

title: Testing the presence of a dormant black hole inside HR 6819
creator: A. Romagnolo A. Olejak A. Hypki G. Wiktorowicz K. Belczynski
description: Abstract Context. HR 6819 was recently reported to be a triple system with a non-accreting black hole (BH). The inner binary system was defined as a B3 III type star (a 5 − 7 ​ M ⊙ 5-7{\rm\penalty\ M}_{\odot} star estimated to be at the end of its main sequence) and a dormant BH ( > 4.

title: DIFFERENTIAL CORRESPONDENCES AND CONTROL THEORY
creator: J.-F. Pommaret
description: Abstract ABSTRACT When a differential field K having n commuting derivations is given together with two finitely generated differential extensions L and M of K , an important problem in differential algebra is to exhibit a common differential extension N in order to define the new differential extensions L\cap M and the smallest differential field (L,M)\subset N containing both L

title: Using automated decision-making (ADM) to allocate Covid-19 vaccinations? Exploring the roles of trust and social group preference on the legitimacy of ADM vs. human decision-making.
creator: Marco Lünich, Kimon Kieslich
description: Abstract In combating the ongoing global health threat of the Covid-19 pandemic, decision-makers have to take actions based on a multitude of relevant health data with severe potential consequences for the affected patients. Because of their presumed advantages in handling and analyzing vast amounts of data, computer systems of automated decision-making (ADM) are implemented and substitute humans in decision-making processes.

title: Singlet Scalars as Dark Matter and the Muon ( g − 2 ) (g-2) Anomaly
creator: Bastián Díaz Sáez, Karim Ghorbani
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Bastián Díaz Sáez, Karim Ghorbani. We explore a simple model containing two singlet scalars as dark matter candidates and a vector-like lepton. Evading collider and dark matter constraints, the model is able to accommodate the correct dark matter relic abundance and the ( g − 2 ) μ (g-2)_{\mu} anomaly when the masses of the three new fields are around 100 GeV and the values of the minimum amount of required couplings are order one.

title: Simple and practical DIQKD security analysis via BB84-type uncertainty relations and Pauli correlation constraints
creator: Michele Masini, Stefano Pironio, Erik Woodhead
description: Abstract According to the entropy accumulation theorem, proving the unconditional security of a device-independent quantum key distribution protocol reduces to deriving tradeoff functions, i.e., bounds on the single-round von Neumann entropy of the raw key as a function of Bell linear functionals, conditioned on an eavesdropper’s quantum side information.

title: Mind the Income Gap: Bias Correction of Inequality Estimators in Small-Sized Samples
creator: Silvia De Nicolò, Maria Rosaria Ferrante, Silvia Pacei
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Silvia De Nicolò, Maria Rosaria Ferrante, Silvia Pacei. Income inequality estimators are biased in small samples, leading generally to an underestimation. This aspect deserves particular attention when estimating inequality in small domains and performing small area estimation at the area level. We propose a bias correction framework for a large class of inequality measures comprising the Gini Index, the Generalized Entropy and the Atkinson index families by accounting for complex survey designs.

title: Integrated shape-sensitive functional metrics Journal: SI of Journal of Multivariate Analysis
creator: Sami Helander, Petra Laketa, Pauliina Ilmonen, Stanislav Nagy ∗, Germain Van Bever, Lauri Viitasaari
description: Abstract This paper develops a new integrated ball (pseudo)metric which provides an intermediary between a chosen starting (pseudo)metric d d and the L p L_{p} distance in general function spaces. Selecting d d as the Hausdorff or Fréchet distances, we introduce integrated shape-sensitive versions of these supremum-based metrics.

title: Investigation of the Carbon Monoxide Dication Lifetime Using (CO) 2 Dimer Fragmentation
creator: A. Méry, X. Fléchard, S. Guillous, V. Kumar, M. Lalande, J. Rangama, W. Wolff, A. Cassimi
description: Abstract The fragmentation of carbon monoxide dimers induced by collisions with low energy Ar 9+ ions is investigated using the COLTRIMS technique. The presence of a neighbor molecule in the dimer serves here as a diagnostic tool to probe the lifetimes of the CO 2 + \rm CO^{2+} molecular dications resulting from the collision.

title: A relative trace formula approach to the Kuznetsov formula on GSp 4 \text{GSp}_{4}
creator: Félicien Comtat
description: Abstract . Relative trace formulas play a central role in studying automorphic forms. In this paper, we use a relative trace formula approach to derive a Kuznetsov type formula for the group GSp 4 \text{GSp}_{4} . We focus on giving a final formula that is as explicit as possible, and we plan on returning to applications elsewhere.

title: Unsupervised Identification of Relevant Prior Cases
creator: Shivangi Bithel, Sumitra S Malagi
description: Abstract . Document retrieval has taken its role in almost all domains of knowledge understanding including the legal domain. Precedent refers to a court decision that is considered as authority for deciding subsequent cases involving identical or similar facts, or similar legal issues.

title: Frequency-Supervised MR-to-CT Image Synthesis
creator: Zenglin Shi 1, Pascal Mettes 1, Guoyan Zheng 2, and Cees Snoek 1
description: Abstract This paper strives to generate a synthetic computed tomography (CT) image from a magnetic resonance (MR) image. The synthetic CT image is valuable for radiotherapy planning when only an MR image is available. Recent approaches have made large strides in solving this challenging synthesis problem with convolutional neural networks that learn a mapping from MR inputs to CT outputs.

title: Intrinsically spherical 3-linked graphs
creator: Madeleine Burkhart, Andrew Castillo, Jonathan Doane, Joel Foisy, Cristopher Negron

title: High-frequency wave power observed in the chromosphere with IBIS and ALMA Facilities: DST(IBIS), ALMA, IRIS SolarSoft ( Freeland & Handy 2012 ) ; Matplotlib ( Hunter 2007 ) ; NumPy ( Oliphant 2006 ) ; SciPy ( Virtanen et al. 2020 ) . The scripts and the Jupyter notebooks containing the code for this
creator: Momchil E. Molnar, Kevin P. Reardon, Steven R. Cranmer, Adam F. Kowalski, Yi Chai, Dale Gary
description: Abstract We present observational constraints on the chromospheric heating contribution from acoustic waves with frequencies between 5 and 50 mHz. We utilize observations from the Dunn Solar Telescope in New Mexico complemented with observations from the Atacama Large Millimeter Array collected on 2017 April 23.

title: Uniform negative immersions and the coherence of one-relator groups
creator: Larsen Louder, Henry Wilton
description: Abstract Previously, the authors proved that the presentation complex of a one-relator group G G satisfies a geometric condition called negative immersions if every two-generator, one-relator subgroup of G G is free. Here, we prove that one-relator groups with negative immersions are coherent, answering a question of Baumslag in this case.

title: OODformer: Out-Of-Distribution Detection Transformer
creator: Rajat Koner, Poulami Sinhamahapatra, Karsten Roscher, Stephan Günnemann, Volker Tresp
description: Abstract A serious problem in image classification is that a trained model might perform well for input data that originates from the same distribution as the data available for model training, but performs much worse for out-of-distribution (OOD) samples. In real-world safety-critical applications, in particular, it is important to be aware if a new data point is OOD.

title: Probing the B + L B+L violation process with the observation of cosmic magnetic field
creator: Yuefeng Di, Jialong Wang, Ligong Bian, Rong-Gen Cai, Jing Liu
description: Abstract We investigate the B + L B+L violation process by performing three-dimensional lattice simulations in an electroweak theory with first-order phase transition and the electroweak sphaleron decay. The simulation results indicate that the Chern-Simons number changes along with the helical magnetic field production when the sphaleron decay occurs.

title: Parametric estimation for functional autoregressive processes on the sphere
creator: Alessia Caponera, Claudio Durastanti
description: Abstract . The aim of this paper is to define a nonlinear least squares estimator for the spectral parameters of a spherical autoregressive process of order 1 in a parametric setting. Furthermore, we investigate on its asymptotic properties, such as weak consistency and asymptotic normality. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary 60G60, 62G05; Secondary 62R30 60G10 1.

title: Semigroup property of fractional differential operators and its applications
creator: N.D. Cong
description: Abstract We establish partial semigroup property of Riemann-Liouville and Caputo fractional differential operators. Using this result we prove theorems on reduction of multi-term fractional differential systems to single-term and multi-order systems, and prove existence and uniqueness of solution to multi-term Caputo fractional differential systems.

title: Hierarchical Few-Shot Imitation with Skill Transition Models
creator: Kourosh Hakhamaneshi, Albert Zhang, Ruihan Zhao, Pieter Abbeel, Michael Laskin
description: Abstract A desirable property of autonomous agents is the ability to both solve long-horizon problems and generalize to unseen tasks. Recent advances in data-driven skill learning have shown that extracting behavioral priors from offline data can enable agents to solve challenging long-horizon tasks with reinforcement learning. However, generalization to tasks unseen during behavioral prior training remains an outstanding challenge.

title: Neural Conditional Reweighting Preprint: MIT-CTP 5315
creator: Benjamin Nachman, Jesse Thaler
description: Abstract There is a growing use of neural network classifiers as unbinned, high-dimensional (and variable-dimensional) reweighting functions. To date, the focus has been on marginal reweighting, where a subset of features are used for reweighting while all other features are integrated over.

title: Causal Inference Struggles with Agency on Online Platforms Conference: 2022 ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency; June 21–24, 2022; Seoul, Republic of Korea 2022 ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency (FAccT ’22), June 21–24, 2022, Seoul, Republic of Kor
creator: Smitha Milli, Luca Belli, Moritz Hardt
description: Abstract . Online platforms regularly conduct randomized experiments to understand how changes to the platform causally affect various outcomes of interest. However, experimentation on online platforms has been criticized for having, among other issues, a lack of meaningful oversight and user consent.

title: The post-transit tail of WASP-107b observed at 10830Å Journal: AJ SciPy ( Virtanen et al. 2020 ) ; NumPy ( Van Der Walt et al. 2011 ) ; matplotlib ( Hunter 2007 ) ; Astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ) , iSpec ( Blanco-Cuaresma et al. 2014 )
creator: J. J. Spake, A. Oklopčić, L. A. Hillenbrand
description: Abstract Understanding the effects of high-energy radiation and stellar winds on planetary atmospheres is vital for explaining the observed properties of close-in exoplanets. Observations of transiting exoplanets in the triplet of metastable helium lines at 10830 Å allow extended atmospheres and escape processes to be studied for individual planets.

title: Spectrum of weak model sets with Borel windows Dedicated to Bob Moody on the occasion of his 80 t ​ h 80^{th} birthday
creator: Gerhard Keller 1 , Christoph Richard 1 and Nicolae Strungaru 2
description: Abstract Consider the extended hull of a weak model set together with its natural shift action. Equip the extended hull with the Mirsky measure, which is a certain natural pattern frequency measure. It is known that the extended hull is a measure-theoretic factor of some group rotation, which is called the underlying torus.

title: Automated free energy calculation from atomistic simulations
creator: Sarath Menon, Yury Lysogorskiy, Jutta Rogal, Ralf Drautz
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Sarath Menon, Yury Lysogorskiy, Jutta Rogal, Ralf Drautz. We devise automated workflows for the calculation of Helmholtz and Gibbs free energies and their temperature and pressure dependence and provide the corresponding computational tools. We employ non-equilibrium thermodynamics for evaluating the free energy of solid and liquid phases at a given temperature and reversible scaling for computing free energies over a wide range of temperatures, including the direct integration of P P - T T coexistence lines.

title: Black Hole Entropy Sourced by String Winding Condensate
creator: Ram Brustein, Yoav Zigdon
description: Abstract We calculate the entropy of an asymptotically Schwarzschild black hole (BH), using an effective field theory of winding modes in type II string theory. In Euclidean signature, the geometry of the black hole contains a thermal cycle which shrinks towards the horizon.

title: A Tree Search Approach for Maximum-Likelihood Decoding of Reed-Muller Codes
creator: Seyyed Ali Hashemi 1 , Nghia Doan 2 , Warren J. Gross 2 , John Cioffi 1 , Andrea Goldsmith 3
description: Abstract A low-complexity tree search approach is presented that achieves the maximum-likelihood (ML) decoding performance of Reed-Muller (RM) codes. The proposed approach generates a bit-flipping tree that is traversed to find the ML decoding result by performing successive-cancellation decoding after each node visit.

title: Generative Design Inspiration for Glyphs with Diatoms
creator: Matthew Brehmer, Robert Kosara, and Carmen Hull
description: Abstract We introduce Diatoms, a technique that generates design inspiration for glyphs by sampling from palettes of mark shapes, encoding channels, and glyph scaffold shapes. Diatoms allows for a degree of randomness while respecting constraints imposed by columns in a data table: their data types and domains as well as semantic associations between columns as specified by the designer.

title: Positive normalized solutions to nonlinear elliptic systems in ℝ 4 \mathbb{R}^{4} with critical Sobolev exponent Thanks: Luo and Yang are supported by NSFC (No. 11901147) and the Fundamental Research Funds for the Central Universities of China (No. JZ2020HGTB0030). Zou is supported by NSFC (No. 2017
