title: Machine learning models for DOTA 2 outcomes prediction
creator: Kodirjon Akhmedov, Anh Huy Phan
description: Abstract Prediction of the real-time multiplayer online battle arena (MOBA) games’ match outcome is one of the most important and exciting tasks in Esports analytical research. This research paper predominantly focuses on building predictive machine and deep learning models to identify the outcome of the Dota 2 MOBA game using the new method of multi-forward steps predictions.

title: Implicit gradients based novel finite volume scheme for compressible single and multi-component flows
creator: Amareshwara Sainadh Chamarthi, Steven H. Frankel, Abhishek Chintagunta
description: Abstract This paper introduces a novel approach to compute the numerical fluxes at the cell boundaries in the finite volume approach. Explicit gradients used in deriving the reconstruction polynomials are replaced by high-order gradients computed by compact finite differences, referred to as implicit gradients in this paper.

title: On the visibility of singularities in general relativity and modified gravity theories
creator: Karim Mosani, Dipanjan Dey, Pankaj S. Joshi, Gauranga C. Samanta, Harikrishnan Menon, Vaishnavi D. Patel
description: Abstract We investigate the global causal structure of the end state of a spherically symmetric marginally bound Lemaitre-Tolman-Bondi (LTB) Lemaitre ; Tolman ; Bondi collapsing cloud (which is well studied in general relativity) in the framework of modified gravity having the generalized Lagrangian R + α ​ R 2 R+\alpha R^{2} in the action.

title: Finite quotients of surface braid groups and double Kodaira fibrations
creator: Francesco Polizzi and Pietro Sabatino
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Francesco Polizzi and Pietro Sabatino. Let Σ b \Sigma_{b} be a closed Riemann surface of genus b b . We give an account of some results obtained in the recent papers CaPol 21 ; Pol 20 ; PolSab 21 and concerning what we call here pure braid quotients , namely non-abelian finite groups appearing as quotients of the pure braid group on two strands 𝖯 2 ​ ( Σ b ) \mathsf{P}_{2}(\Sigma_{b}) .

title: Anomalous and Anisotropic Nonlinear Susceptibility in the Proximate Kitaev Magnet α \alpha -RuCl 3
creator: Ludwig Holleis 1, Joseph Prestigiacomo 2, Zhijie Fan 1, Satoshi Nishimoto 3, Mike Osofsky 2, Gia-Wei Chern 1, Jeroen van den Brink 3,4, B.S. Shivaram 1
description: Abstract The leading order nonlinear (NL) susceptibility, χ 3 \chi_{3} , in a paramagnet is negative and diverges as T → 0 T\rightarrow 0 . This divergence is destroyed when spins correlate and the NL response provides unique insights into magnetic order. Dimensionality, exchange interaction, and preponderance of quantum effects all imprint their signatures in the NL magnetic response.

title: What Happened Next? Using Deep Learning to Value Defensive Actions in Football Event-Data Conference: Proceedings of the 27th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining; August 14–18, 2021; Virtual Event, Singapore Proceedings of the 27th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discover
creator: Charbel Merhej, Ryan J Beal, Tim Matthews, Sarvapali Ramchurn
description: Abstract . Objectively quantifying the value of player actions in football (soccer) is a challenging problem. To date, studies in football analytics have mainly focused on the attacking side of the game, while there has been less work on event-driven metrics for valuing defensive actions (e.g., tackles and interceptions).

title: Interacting Swarm Sensing and Stabilization
creator: Ira B. Schwartz, Victoria Edwards, Jason Hindes
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Ira B. Schwartz, Victoria Edwards, Jason Hindes. Swarming behavior, where coherent motion emerges from the interactions of many mobile agents, is ubiquitous in physics and biology. Moreover, there are many efforts to replicate swarming dynamics in mobile robotic systems which take inspiration from natural swarms. In particular, understanding how swarms come apart, change their behavior, and interact with other swarms is a research direction of special interest to the robotics and defense communities.

title: A Computer Program for the Numerical Analysis of Economic Cycles Within the Framework of the Dubovsky Generalized Model
creator: Makarov Danil, Parovik Roman
description: Abstract The article proposes a computer program for calculating economic crises according to the generalized mathematical model of S.V. Dubovsky. This model is represented by a system of ordinary nonlinear differential equations with fractional derivatives in the sense of Gerasimov-Caputo with initial conditions.

title: Defending Against Backdoor Attacks in Natural Language Generation
creator: Xiaofei Sun, Xiaoya Li, Yuxian Meng, Xiang Ao, Lingjuan Lyu, Jiwei Li, Tianwei Zhang
description: Abstract The frustratingly fragile nature of neural network models make current natural language generation (NLG) systems prone to backdoor attacks and generate malicious sequences that could be sexist or offensive. Unfortunately, little effort has been invested to how backdoor attacks can affect current NLG models and how to defend against these attacks.

title: Поступила в редакцию
description: Abstract Краткие сообщения УДК 515.122.4 Непрерывность обратного в группах Е. А. Резниченко 1 1 1 Резниченко Евгений Александрович — канд. физ.-мат. наук, доцент каф. общей топологии и геометрии мех.-мат. ф-та МГУ, e-mail: erezn@inbox.ru. Reznichenko Evgenii Aleksandrovich — Candidate of Physical and Mathematical Sciences, Associate Professor, Lomonosov Moscow State University, Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics, Chair of General Topology and Geometry.

title: Detecting ergodic bubbles at the crossover to many-body localization using neural networks
creator: Tomasz Szołdra, Piotr Sierant, Korbinian Kottmann, Maciej Lewenstein, Jakub Zakrzewski
description: Abstract The transition between ergodic and many-body localized phases is expected to occur via an avalanche mechanism, in which ergodic bubbles that arise due to local fluctuations in system properties thermalize their surroundings leading to delocalization of the system, unless the disorder is sufficiently strong to stop this process.

title: DNA-GCN: Graph convolutional networks for predicting DNA-protein binding
creator: Yuhang Guo, Xiao Luo, Liang Chen, Minghua Deng
description: Abstract Predicting DNA-protein binding is an important and classic problem in bioinformatics. Convolutional neural networks have outperformed conventional methods in modeling the sequence specificity of DNA-protein binding. However, none of the studies has utilized graph convolutional networks for motif inference. In this work, we propose to use graph convolutional networks for motif inference.

title: On the Role of Out-of-Equilibrium Phonons in Gated Superconducting Switches
creator: M. F. Ritter, N. Crescini, D. Z. Haxell, M. Hinderling, H. Riel, C. Bruder, A. Fuhrer, F. Nichele
description: Abstract Recent experiments suggest the possibility to tune superconductivity in metallic nanowires by application of modest gate voltages. It is largely debated whether the effect is due to an electric field at the superconductor surface or small currents of high-energy electrons.

title: Internal Shortest Absent Word Queries in Constant Time and Linear Space Note: The present paper is an extended and improved version of an earlier text that appeared in the 32nd Annual Symposium on Combinatorial Pattern Matching, CPM 2021 [ 8 ] .
creator: Golnaz Badkobeh, Panagiotis Charalampopoulos, Dmitry Kosolobov, Solon P. Pissis
description: Abstract Given a string T T of length n n over an alphabet Σ ⊂ { 1 , 2 , … , n 𝒪 ⁡ ( 1 ) } \Sigma\subset\{1,2,\ldots,n^{\mathcal{O}(1)}\} of size σ \sigma , we are to preprocess T T so that given a range [ i , j ] [i,j] , we can return a representation of a

title: A note on the Compactness of Poincaré-Einstein manifolds Thanks: Wang and Zhou’s research are supported in part by National Natural Science Foundation of China No. 11871331 and Shanghai Science and Technology Innovation Action Plan No. 20JC1413100.
creator: Fang Wang, Huihuang Zhou
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Fang Wang, Huihuang Zhou. For a conformally compact Poincaré-Einstein manifold ( X , g + ) (X,g_{+}) , we consider two types of compactifications for it. One is g ¯ = ρ 2 ​ g + \bar{g}=\rho^{2}g_{+} , where ρ \rho is a fixed smooth defining function; the other is the adapted (including Fefferman-Graham) compactification g ¯ s = ρ s 2 ​ g + \bar{g}_{s}=\rho^{2}_{s}g_{+} with a continuous parameter s > n 2 s>\frac{n}{2} .

title: LiMIIRL: Lightweight Multiple-Intent Inverse Reinforcement Learning
creator: Aaron J. Snoswell, Surya P. N. Singh, Nan Ye
description: Abstract Multiple-Intent Inverse Reinforcement Learning (MI-IRL) seeks to find a reward function ensemble to rationalize demonstrations of different but unlabelled intents. Within the popular expectation maximization (EM) framework for learning probabilistic MI-IRL models, we present a warm-start strategy based on up-front clustering of the demonstrations in feature space.

title: Explaining Recruitment to Extremism: A Bayesian Case-Control Approach
creator: Roberto Cerina, Christopher Barrie, Neil Ketchley, Aaron Y. Zelin
description: Abstract Who joins extremist movements? Answering this question poses considerable methodological challenges. Survey techniques are infeasible and selective samples provide no counterfactual. Recruits can be assigned to contextual units, but this is vulnerable to problems of ecological inference. In this article, we take inspiration from epidemiology and elaborate a technique that combines survey and ecological approaches.

title: Deep Learning Based Analysis of Prostate Cancer from MP-MRI
creator: Pedro David Carneiro Neto
description: Abstract Master’s Programme in Computer, Communication and Information Sciences Deep Learning Based Analysis of Prostate Cancer from MP-MRI Classification, detection and segmentation of prostate cancer lesions from MP-MRI with deep learning based methods Pedro David Carneiro Neto MASTER’S THESIS \AaltoLogoSmall .66?

title: The dynamic effect of mechanical losses of transmissions on the equation of motion of legged robots
creator: Youngwoo Sim, Joao Ramos
description: Abstract Industrial manipulators do not collapse under their own weight when powered off due to the friction in their joints. Although these mechanism are effective for stiff position control of pick-and-place, they are inappropriate for legged robots that must rapidly regulate compliant interactions with the environment.

title: Environment driven oscillation in an off-lattice May–Leonard model
creator: D. Bazeia, M. J. B. Ferreira, B.F. de Oliveira, A. Szolnoki
description: Abstract Cyclic dominance of competing species is an intensively used working hypothesis to explain biodiversity in certain living systems, where the evolutionary selection principle would dictate a single victor otherwise. Technically the May–Leonard models offer a mathematical framework to describe the mentioned non-transitive interaction of competing species when individual movement is also considered in a spatial system.

title: Optimization-Based Algebraic Multigrid Coarsening Using Reinforcement Learning
creator: Ali Taghibakhshi, Scott MacLachlan, Luke Olson, Matthew West
description: Abstract Large sparse linear systems of equations are ubiquitous in science and engineering, such as those arising from discretizations of partial differential equations. Algebraic multigrid (AMG) methods are one of the most common methods of solving such linear systems, with an extensive body of underlying mathematical theory.

title: Macrospin model of an assembly of magnetically coupled core-shell nanoparticles
creator: Nikolaos Ntallis, Corisa Kons, Hariharan Srikanth, Manh-Huong Phan, D.A. Arena, Manuel Pereiro
description: Abstract Highly sophisticated synthesis methods and experimental techniques allow for precise measurements of magnetic properties of nanoparticles that can be reliably reproduced using theoretical models. Here, we investigate the magnetic properties of ferrite nanoparticles by using theoretical techniques based on Monte Carlo methods. We introduce three stages of sophistication in the macromagnetic model.

title: Separated-Spectral-Distribution Estimation Based on Bayesian Inference with Single RGB Camera
creator: Yuma Kinoshita, Hitoshi Kiya
description: Abstract In this paper, we propose a novel method for separately estimating spectral distributions from images captured by a typical RGB camera. The proposed method allows us to separately estimate a spectral distribution of illumination, reflectance, or camera sensitivity, while recent hyperspectral cameras are limited to capturing a joint spectral distribution from a scene.

title: Continual learning in Deep Neural Networks: an Analysis of the Last Layer
creator: Timothée Lesort, Thomas George, Irina Rish
description: Abstract We study how different output layer parameterizations of a deep neural network affects learning and forgetting in continual learning settings. The following three effects can cause catastrophic forgetting in the output layer: (1) weights modifications, (2) interference, and (3) projection drift.

title: Corruption in Auctions: Social Welfare Loss in Hybrid Multi-Unit Auctions
creator: Andries van Beek, Ruben Brokkelkamp, Guido Schäfer
description: Abstract We initiate the study of the social welfare loss caused by corrupt auctioneers, both in single-item and multi-unit auctions. In our model, the auctioneer may collude with the winning bidders by letting them lower their bids in exchange for a (possibly bidder-dependent) fraction γ \gamma of the surplus. We consider different corruption schemes.

title: A Finsler counterexample to the Croke conjecture for the systolic ratio on the 2-sphere Thanks: The first author acknowledges support by SNSF grant Metric geometry and Finsler structures of low regularity number 200021L-175985, the second by RWTH University. Both authors would like to thank Prof. Um
creator: Guillaume Buro and Louis Merlin
description: Abstract . We exhibit a Finsler metric on the 2 2 -sphere whose systolic (Holmes-Thompson) ratio is 4 ​ π 3 \frac{4\pi}{3} . This is bigger than the conjectured maximal Riemannian systolic ratio of 2 ​ 3 2\sqrt{3} achieved by the Calabi-Croke metric. The construction of the Finsler metric is heavily inspired by [ CS20 ] .

title: Heart Sound Classification Considering Additive Noise and Convolutional Distortion
creator: FARHAT BINTE AZAM, MD. ISTIAQ ANSARI, IAN MCLANE, AND TAUFIQ HASAN
description: Abstract Cardiac auscultation is an essential point-of-care method used for the early diagnosis of heart diseases. Automatic analysis of heart sounds for abnormality detection is faced with the challenges of additive noise and sensor-dependent degradation. This paper aims to develop methods to address the cardiac abnormality detection problem when both types of distortions are present in the cardiac auscultation sound.

title: Diffusion, phase behavior and gelation in a two-dimensional layer of colloids in osmotic equilibrium with a polymer reservoir
creator: Sam E. Griffiths, Nick Koumakis, Aidan T. Brown, Teun Vissers, Patrick B. Warren, Wilson C. K. Poon
description: Abstract The addition of enough non-adsorbing polymer to an otherwise stable colloidal suspension gives rise to a variety of phase behavior and kinetic arrest due to the depletion attraction induced between the colloids by the polymers. We report a study of these phenomena in a two-dimensional layer of colloids.

title: Transient Optoplasmonic Detection of Single Proteins with Sub-Microsecond Resolution
creator: Martin D. Baaske, N. Asgari, D. Punj, Michel Orrit

title: Optimal laser focusing for positron production in laser-electron scattering
creator: Óscar Amaro, Marija Vranic
description: Abstract Laser-electron beam collisions that aim to generate electron-positron pairs require laser intensities I ≳ 10 21 I\gtrsim 10^{21} W/cm 2 , which can be obtained by focusing a 1-PW optical laser to a spot smaller than 10 μ \mu m.

title: Global solutions of 2D isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations with one slow variable
creator: Yong Lu, Ping Zhang
description: Abstract . Motivated by [ 2 , 3 ] , we prove the global existence of solutions to the two-dimensional isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations with smooth initial data which are slowly varying in one direction and with initial density being away from vacuum.

title: How can gravitational-wave standard sirens and 21-cm intensity mapping jointly provide a precise late-universe cosmological probe?
creator: Shang-Jie Jin, Ling-Feng Wang, Peng-Ju Wu, Jing-Fei Zhang, Xin Zhang
description: Abstract In the next decades, the gravitational-wave (GW) standard siren observations and the neutral hydrogen 21-cm intensity mapping (IM) surveys, as two promising cosmological probes, will play an important role in precisely measuring cosmological parameters. In this work, we make a forecast for cosmological parameter estimation with the synergy between the GW standard siren observations and the 21-cm IM surveys.

title: Strong coupling regime and hybrid quasinormal modes of a single plasmonic resonator coupled to a TMDC monolayer
creator: Chelsea Carlson, Robert Salzwedel, Malte Selig, Andreas Knorr, Stephen Hughes
description: Abstract We present a rigorous photonic mode model to describe the strong coupling between a monolayer of MoSe 2 \rm MoSe_{2} and a single gold nanoparticle. The onset of strong coupling is quantified by computing the three-dimensional hybrid quasinormal modes of the combined structure, allowing one to accurately model light-matter interactions without invoking the usual phenomenological theories of strong coupling.

title: Averaging Principle for Backward Stochastic Differential Equations driven by both standard and fractional Brownian motions
creator: Ibrahima Faye, Sadibou Aidara, Yaya Sagna
description:
A 2021 arXiv research paper by Ibrahima Faye, Sadibou Aidara, Yaya Sagna. Stochastic averaging for a class of backward stochastic differential equations driven by both standard and fractional Brownian motions (SFrBSDEs in short), is investigated. An averaged SFrBSDEs for the original SFrBSDEs is proposed, and their solutions are quantitatively compared. Under some appropriate assumptions, the solutions to original systems can be approximated by the solutions to averaged stochastic systems in the sense of mean square and also in probability. 1
Université Alioune Diop de Bambey, BP.

title: CONVOLUTIONAL NEURAL NETWORK IN STOCK PRICE MOVEMENT PREDICTION
creator: Kunal Bhardwaj
description: Abstract The usability of Neural Networks in different sectors has been a hot topic of research for many years. With technological advancements and exponential growth of data, we have been unfolding different capabilities of neural networks in different sectors. In this paper, I have tried to use CONVOLUTIONAL NEURAL NETWORK in STOCK PRICE MOVEMENT PREDICTION.

title: Construction of New Solutions to Field Equations by Using one Non–Separable Solution and one Symmetry of the System
creator: Sergio A. Hojman
description: Abstract Symmetries of the field equations are used to construct infinitely many non–trivial linearly independent new solutions to different partial differential equations such as the Schrödinger, the diffusion, and the paraxial equations, among many others, including Klein–Gordon, Dirac, Maxwell, Rarita–Schwinger and linear Einstein field equations (and even some especial seed solutions of fully non-linear General Relativity).

title: Conformal Prediction Bands
creator: for Multivariate Functional Data
description: Abstract Abstract Motivated by the pressing request of methods able to create prediction sets in a general regression framework for a multivariate functional response and pushed by new methodological advancements in non-parametric prediction for functional data, we propose a set of conformal predictors that produce finite-sample either valid or exact multivariate simultaneous prediction bands under the mild assumption of exchangeable

title: Search for chargino–neutralino pair production in final states with three leptons and missing transverse momentum in s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13 TeV p ​ p pp collisions with the ATLAS detector
creator: The ATLAS Collaboration
description: Abstract A search for chargino–neutralino pair production in three-lepton final states with missing transverse momentum is presented. The study is based on a dataset of s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13 TeV p ​ p pp collisions recorded with the ATLAS detector at the LHC, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 139 fb -1 .

title: Near Optimal Stochastic Algorithms for Finite-Sum Unbalanced Convex-Concave Minimax Optimization
creator: Luo Luo, Guangzeng Xie Tong Zhang Zhihua Zhang
description: Abstract This paper considers stochastic first-order algorithms for convex-concave minimax problems of the form min 𝐱 ⁡ max 𝐲 ⁡ f ⁡ ( 𝐱 , 𝐲 ) \min_{\bf x}\max_{\bf y}f(\bf x,\bf y) , where f f can be presented by the average of n n individual components which are L L -average smooth.

title: GL-GIN: Fast and Accurate Non-Autoregressive Model for Joint Multiple Intent Detection and Slot Filling
creator: Libo Qin, Fuxuan Wei, Tianbao Xie, Xiao Xu, Wanxiang Che, Ting Liu
description: Abstract Multi-intent SLU can handle multiple intents in an utterance, which has attracted increasing attention. However, the state-of-the-art joint models heavily rely on autoregressive approaches, resulting in two issues: slow inference speed and information leakage . In this paper, we explore a non-autoregressive model for joint multiple intent detection and slot filling, achieving more fast and accurate.

title: Enhancing the effective critical current density in a Nb superconducting thin film by cooling in an inhomogeneous magnetic field
creator: D. A. D. Chaves, I. M. de Araújo, D. Carmo, F. Colauto, A. A. M. de Oliveira, A. M. H. de Andrade, T. H. Johansen, A. V. Silhanek, W. A. Ortiz, M. Motta
description: Abstract Quantitative magneto-optical imaging of a type-II superconductor thin film cooled under zero, homogeneous, and inhomogeneous applied magnetic fields, indicates that the latter procedure leads to an enhancement of the screening capacity. Such an observation is corroborated by both B B -independent and B B -dependent critical state model analyses.

title: A biased MC for muon production for beam-dump experiments Dedication: To be submitted to EPJ C
creator: Stefan Ghinescu, Babette Döbrich, Elisa Minucci, Tommaso Spadaro
description: Abstract The search for feebly-interacting new-physics particles in the MeV-GeV mass range often involves high-intensity beams dumped into thick heavy targets. The challenge of evaluating the expected backgrounds for these searches from first principles is limited by the CPU time needed to generate the shower induced by the primary beam.

title: Can one hear a matrix? Recovering a real symmetric matrix from its spectral data
creator: Uzy Smilansky
description: Abstract The spectrum of a real and symmetric N × N N\times N matrix determines the matrix up to unitary equivalence. More spectral data is needed together with some sign indicators to remove the unitary ambiguities. In the first part of this work we specify the spectral and sign information required for a unique reconstruction of general matrices.

title: Supercurrent diode effect and finite momentum superconductivity
creator: Noah F. Q. Yuan 1,2, Liang Fu 2∗
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Noah F. Q. Yuan 1,2, Liang Fu 2∗. When both inversion and time-reversal symmetries are broken, the critical current of a superconductor can be nonreciprocal. In this work we show that in certain classes of two-dimensional superconductors with antisymmetric spin-orbit coupling, Cooper pairs acquire a finite momentum upon the application of an in-plane magnetic field, and as a result, critical currents in the direction parallel and antiparallel to the Cooper pair momentum become unequal.
